stories.title: Democrat Hubbard wins North Carolina recount, clinching historic House majority
stories.description: Democrat Chuck Hubbard was elected to the US House of Representatives from North Carolina on Sunday after defeating veteran Republican Virginia Foxx, who chairs the powerful House Rules Committee. His victory gave Democrats their best general election result in decades, winning at least 258 seats in the 2026 US midterms.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Russian warship hit by suspected Ukrainian drone at Benghazi naval base, Libyan officials say
stories.description: A Russian navy corvette docked at the Benghazi naval base ​in eastern Libya was hit on Sunday by a suspected Ukrainian sea drone, according to local officials. The strike severely damaged the warship and ignited a fire at the facility in what appeared to be the latest attack in Libya linked to the Russia-Ukraine war.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Burnham, 'Brejoin' & the Ghosts of Brexit
stories.description: “The people of Britain have spoken, and the answer is: we are out.” The words of David Dimbleby at 4.40am on 24 June 2016, as the Brexit referendum result became clear. But nearly a decade on, is Britain changing its mind? Prime Minister Andy Burnham has reopened talks with Brussels, exploring options for a closer relationship with the EU. But the move has drawn criticism from key figures behind Brexit, including Theresa May and Boris Johnson. So what is driving this rethink, and where might it lead? France 24's Gavin Lee speaks to John McTernan, veteran Labour strategist and former adviser to Tony Blair.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Le Pen denies receiving leaked information from French interior ministry official
stories.description: French far-right leader Marine Le Pen on Sunday said she did not receive, nor ask for, confidential information on an investigation into her party from a senior interior ministry official. She however could not say if other party members had benefited from the leaks. Hugues Moutouh, the civil servant under suspicion, has denied the allegations and asked to be relieved of his duties pending a probe.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Ligue 1: PSG extend winning run at Nice (3-2) but lose Désiré Doué to injury
stories.description: A bittersweet victory for PSG at Nice on Saturday evening. The Parisians strengthened their grip on top spot in Ligue 1, but lost Désiré Doué for several months after the forward suffered a serious knee injury.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Drone strikes hit homes and UN building in Sudan's Khartoum
stories.description: Drone strikes damaged residential homes and a United Nations building in Sudan's capital Khartoum early Sunday, with the army accusing neighbouring Ethiopia of launching the attacks. The strikes came as drone warfare intensifies in the country's conflict, now in its fourth year.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: West Bank attacks: Opposition leader Eisenkot decries "Jewish terrorism"
stories.description: Israeli authorities have opened an investigation after Palestinian vehicles and properties were set on fire in three villages in the occupied West Bank. Israeli soldiers were deployed to the area following the attacks, which local residents said were carried out by Israeli settlers. Gadi Eisenkot, a rival of outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, condemned the acts on X, describing them as “Jewish terrorism”. Antonia Kerrigan reports.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Russian strike kills 2 in Kyiv
stories.description: A Russian attack struck an apartment building in the village of Dymer, just north of Kyiv, on Sunday, killing at least two people and wounding four others. The morning strike destroyed a five-storey building, while rescuers evacuated nine people, including a child. At least 11 others are believed to remain trapped under the rubble.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: The week in pictures: Xi hosts Trump and Putin, COP31 and new French protests
stories.description: From the unprecedented Shenzhen summit in China that saw President Xi Jinping host his US and Russian counterparts, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, to tough talks at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey and another week of French protests over the cost of living, FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the most striking images from the past week.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: "It can take years": Why the AI Riemann proof is far from settled
stories.description: AI claimed another major scalp in maths on Friday, as Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge published what he says is a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, a Millennium Prize Problem, in 17 million lines of code that no human has read in full. Physicist Tony Padilla tells Tech 24 that verification could take years, and that Alpöge should share how he got there.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Israel investigates West Bank fires
stories.description: Israeli authorities have opened an investigation after Palestinian vehicles and properties were vandalised and set on fire in four villages in the occupied West Bank, in attacks local activists say were carried out by Israeli settlers. Around eight vehicles were reportedly torched and racist slogans sprayed on walls, prompting Israeli soldiers and police to deploy to the area. The attacks come amid a surge in settler violence since the outbreak of the Gaza war in October 2023, with more than 1,100 Palestinians killed by Israeli soldiers or settlers in the West Bank since then, according to an AFP tally. They also follow recent sanctions announced by the UK and Australia against eight Israeli companies involved in settlement activity. France 24 correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky shares further details from Jerusalem.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 🔴 COP31 ends without deal as EU rejects text for omitting mention of fossil fuels
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Indonesia factory hit by deadly blaze: Three killed and 36 missing
stories.description: At least three people have been killed and dozens are missing after a fire broke out at a factory in Indonesia producing sweets and snack products. Fifteen people were rescued alive from the plant, while firefighters were still battling flames in several parts of the facility more than 12 hours after the blaze began. The cause of the fire remains unknown, but survivors said it started in a cooling unit on the third floor.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Former Italian police chief found dead
stories.description: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has expressed shock following the death of a former national police chief, whose body was found on Saturday. He had been under investigation over an alleged cover-up in an inquiry into a bombing linked to organised crime in Sicily. Jennie Shin reports.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Princess of Wales opens up about cancer
stories.description: A new documentary titled Heal follows Britain’s Princess Catherine as she navigates life since her cancer diagnosis in 2024. The film tracks the 44-year-old as she attempts to climb the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales within 24 hours. In the trailer, she reflects on healing as a journey. Ophelie Jacobson reports.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: South Korea: AI cheating sparks exam security chaos
stories.description: South Korea’s education minister resigned on Sunday following a major cheating scandal that erupted just ahead of the country’s university entrance exams. The controversy centred on the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam, who admitted to using a miniature camera and smartphone to secure a near-perfect result. Jack Pownall reports.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Europe sees new protests over rising costs, inequality and public services
stories.description: Sunday marks the third consecutive day of protests across Europe, following large demonstrations on Friday and smaller rallies on Saturday, from Portugal to France. The protests have largely focused on the rising cost of living and access to affordable housing. In France, demonstrations have now taken place for six weekends in a row. Ophelie Jacobson reports.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: English village votes to "leave UK"
stories.description: Residents of the small English village of Barnham voted on Saturday in a symbolic referendum to leave the UK, in protest against government plans to house 931 asylum seekers at a nearby former air force base – more than the village’s own population of 584. The vote follows a similar protest in another village in September, highlighting growing tensions over immigration across the country. Earlier this week, the leader of a far-right anti-immigration group was jailed, but supporters have vowed to keep the movement alive. Jack Pownall reports.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: NATO faces sovereignty dilemma as militaries rely on private tech, AI
stories.description: NATO officials and defence experts gathered at the NATO Edge conference in Turkey this week to discuss how militaries can harness artificial intelligence and high tech without compromising control over sensitive data and defence capabilities.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Live: At least 14 feared trapped after Russian strike in Kyiv region, Zelensky says
stories.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said at least 14 people were missing after a Russian drone struck a five-story residential building in Dymer, in the Kyiv region, injuring two others. Meanwhile, Finland warned the war was "spilling over" after a drone set fire to a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea on Saturday. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: South Korean education minister resigns over AI-driven exam cheating scandal
stories.description: South Korea Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned Sunday over an AI-assisted cheating scandal that erupted days before the high-stakes Suneung university entrance exam. The Suneung concluded "without any major incidents" last week, Choi said, but he admitted to a failure to "prepare adequately in advance".
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Bahrain accuses Iran of striking industrial site as tankers hit in Hormuz
stories.description: Bahrain accused Iran of striking a civilian industrial site on Saturday evening, as two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran reported shooting down a US drone amid stalled efforts to end the war.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: EU-Indonesia agreement sees the light after ten years of negotiations
stories.description: The European Union and Indonesia have signed a major trade deal, ten years after talks began.The agreement removes almost all tariffs between the EU and Southeast Asia's biggest economy: 98.5 per cent of them. For Europe, it means access to a market of 280 million people and a steadier supply of nickel for batteries. For Indonesia, easier exports of palm oil, textiles and footwear, and it arrives just before its current EU trade preferences end on the 1st of January. To discuss the deal Airlangga Hartarto, Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs in Indonesia joined us on the programme.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu’s party for ‘marathon’ Israeli coalition talks
stories.description: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has invited caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party for coalition talks, his centrist Yashar party said Saturday. The "marathon series of talks" starts Sunday, the party said, adding that the move reflected a commitment to form "the broadest possible government" after the October election failed to deliver an outright winner.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: France’s sixth consecutive Saturday of protests draw lower turnout
stories.description: Turnout ⁠was down ​at largely peaceful demonstrations across France on the sixth consecutive Saturday of protests ​over the cost of living, with the interior ministry putting the figure at 82,500 across the country. Organisers said 150,000 people participated in the nationwide protests, down from their 200,000 figure last week.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: 'Worst Ever' COP Summit?
stories.description: Is this the worst COP summit on record? With limited political leadership, no official US delegation and mounting frustration over bureaucratic delays, questions are being raised about the effectiveness of the climate negotiations. Juan Carlos Beldsoe, a former White House climate adviser under Bill Clinton, described the process as labyrinthine and ultimately dispiriting. France 24's Gavin Lee speaks with climate advocate and six-time COP delegate, Henna Hundal about what this means for the future of global climate action.
stories.subject: Climate

stories.title: Russia attacks Zelensky's hometown, Ukraine reaffirms wish to join NATO
stories.description: A Russian ballistic missile attack on President Volodymyr Zelensky’s hometown in central Ukraine on Saturday killed two people and wounded dozens. Hours later, Zelensky reiterated his country's determination to join NATO, following proposals to provide Kyiv with security guarantees similar to those of the military alliance.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Russia launches ballistic missile attack on Zelensky's hometown in central Ukraine
stories.description: A Russian ballistic missile attack on President Volodymyr Zelensky’s hometown in central Ukraine on Saturday killed two people and wounded dozens. Hours later, Zelensky reiterated his country's determination to join NATO. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Kyiv.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Drone attack sets Russian cargo ship ablaze in Gulf of Finland
stories.description: A Russian cargo ship caught fire after ​being hit by drones in the Baltic Sea on Saturday and drifted into Finnish waters. Reporting from Kyiv, FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg notes that the ship is affiliated with a major Russian military logistics company. While Ukrainian authorities typically neither confirm nor deny responsibility, analysts cite a clear motive for the targeting, Cragg explains.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: COP31: Deep divisions persist over energy, finance and science
stories.description: COP31 climate talks in Turkey have gone into overtime, with deep divisions over fossil fuels, climate finance and global warming targets delaying an agreement. A revised draft dropped all mention of fossil fuels, prompting strong criticism from the EU and a dozen countries demanding a clear commitment to phase them out. Negotiators are also split over a proposed global electrification target, carbon capture and the future of UN climate science reports. Developing nations have voiced anger over the removal of a $120 billion climate adaptation funding target. Australia is now racing to secure a revised deal before delegates leave. France 24 journalist Adria Rocha Cutiller tells us the latest.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: FBI criminal database hacked
stories.description: The FBI is investigating a reported major cyberattack targeting its national law enforcement database, the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which holds sensitive criminal justice records, including information on fugitives, missing persons, criminal histories and stolen property. President Donald Trump said he had just been briefed on the incident, describing it as “not good”. FRANCE 24’s Fraser Jackson reports from Washington DC.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Man convicted of starting palisades fire
stories.description: A Los Angeles County jury found former rideshare driver Jonathan Rinderknecht guilty on Friday of starting the 2025 Palisades fire, which caused widespread destruction and loss of life. He faces a prison sentence of between five and 40 years. Liza Kaminov has more.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: French police officers convicted of racist assault
stories.description: A French court on Friday sentenced three policemen to serve time over the beating of a black music producer in 2020. It also recognized the assault on Michelle Zecler was racially motivated.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Endurance athlete swims in Hormuz Strait
stories.description: The Strait of Hormuz remains largely blocked, with Iran attacking vessels attempting to cross it. As concerns grow over the environmental impact of the war, with toxic chemicals spreading through the air and sea, one swimmer and ocean advocate has gone a step further than issuing warnings: he plunged into the polluted and dangerous waters of the strait, calling on all sides to end the conflict.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: France: Demonstrations losing steam as movement enters sixth week
stories.description: Around 2,200 people took part in protests across France by 2pm local time, according to the Interior Ministry, which recorded 44 demonstrations nationwide and seven arrests, with the situation described as generally calm. Turnout was lower than on previous Saturdays. Reporting from Place de la République in Paris, FRANCE 24’s Antonia Kerrigan said rent rights organisations had also joined the sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, highlighting their growing pan-European dimension, with demonstrations taking place in seven European countries, including Spain, Portugal, Greece and Germany, where rising living costs and access to affordable housing are among the main concerns.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Countries race to secure Cop31 deal
stories.description: COP31 climate talks have overrun their schedule as countries race to agree on a new global climate deal, following criticism of an earlier draft that made no mention of fossil fuels. The EU has warned that the current proposal risks turning the summit into a “fossil fuel summit”, as negotiators work towards a revised, potentially final agreement expected later today. France 24 International affairs editor Jamie Smith-Maillet tells us more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: New day of protests across France
stories.description: France faces a sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, with demonstrators taking to the streets to rally over the rising cost of living and the government's handling of weeks of social unrest ahead of next year's presidential election. France 24 journalist Antonia Kerrigan tells us more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Mexico captures drug cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’ after deadly firefight
stories.description: Mexico's military forces captured ​one of the most wanted suspected drug lords, Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro," the military announced on Saturday, after a deadly firefight that killed seven suspected attackers and four soldiers. Flores, one of the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives, was flown to Mexico City after his capture.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Cargo ship runs aground off French coast
stories.description: A Maltese-flagged cargo ship remains stranded off the coast of south-western France after running aground. French authorities are preparing an operation to prevent the vessel from capsizing and potentially causing pollution. The ship was not carrying any cargo, and all 19 crew members were safely evacuated by helicopter. Dan Quinlan reports.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Russia tests NATO’s eastern defences
stories.description: Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland on Friday in what Prime Minister Donald Tusk said was likely an "intentional provocation" timed to coincide with European military exercises in the country for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine. Senior Lecturer in Conflict and Security at King's College in London, Domitilla Sagramoso, shares further insights.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Thousands protest overs prices, education, military spending in France and Europe
stories.description: France is bracing for a sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, with demonstrators expected to rally over the rising cost of living and the government's handling of weeks of social unrest ahead of next year's presidential election. France 24 journalist Antonia Kerrigan tells us the latest from Paris.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Drone attack sets Russian cargo ship ablaze in Gulf of Finland
stories.description: A Russian cargo ship caught fire after a drone strike in international waters in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday and later drifted into Finnish ⁠territorial waters, Finnish authorities said. Helsinki alerted NATO and imposed temporary restrictions in the area amid heightened tensions in the Baltic Sea.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Ethiopia: Tackling period poverty and stigma
stories.description: In Ethiopia, entrepreneur Hanan Ahmed is tackling period poverty and the stigma surrounding menstruation. By producing affordable reusable sanitary pads and raising awareness in schools, she hopes to make menstrual health more accessible and help girls stay in class. Report by Awa Diouf & Guillaume Gougeon.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Ethiopia - Eritrea: Troops mobilise along the border
stories.description: More than 200 former Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) fighters surrendered to Ethiopia’s federal military Friday, state-affiliated media reported, amid escalating border tensions with neighboring Eritrea. France 24 correspondent Tom Canetti tells us the latest.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Music strikes a chord at French protest
stories.description: Throughout history, protest songs have brought people together across genres, rallying against war, racism, inequality and the establishment. Music is also playing a key role in the youth-led demonstrations here in France. Our reporters went to meet some of the musicians using their voices to express the protesters’ demands.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'Accept cookies'? Russia collects data from swaths of unknowing Swedes
stories.description: A Russian tech firm backed by an oligarch close to President Vladimir Putin has secretly been collecting data from hundreds of thousands – possibly millions – of Swedes, a newspaper investigation found. The revelation has rattled the Nordic nation, whose proximity to Russia and unusually open public records system make it particularly vulnerable to Moscow’s hybrid war tactics.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'Unacceptable': EU chief condemns alleged Russian plot to kill US-Ukrainian citizen
stories.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned an alleged Russian intelligence plot to assassinate a US-Ukrainian citizen in Denmark, vowing full solidarity with Copenhagen.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Was Vladimir Putin 'snubbed' by Xi Jinping? Viral handshake video is AI fake
stories.description: A viral video appearing to show China's Xi Jinping "snubbing" Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit has racked up millions of views, fuelling speculation about tensions between Beijing and Moscow. But the footage is fake. FRANCE 24 traced the original video to an earlier summit, where the two leaders did shake hands. The creator, who runs a satire account, admitted to manipulating the footage using Grok Imagine, an AI tool developed by Elon Musk's xAI, as Vedika Bahl explains.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Denmark accuses Russia of assassination plot, expels diplomat
stories.description: Denmark has accused Moscow of being behind a failed assassination attempt targeting a Ukrainian-American rapper in Copenhagen, further escalating tensions between Europe and Russia. In response, Danish authorities have ordered the expulsion of a Russian diplomat and announced tighter restrictions on visas for Russian tourists. Yuka Royer reports.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Houthis launch strikes on Saudi Arabia
stories.description: Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen continue to exchange strikes with the Saudi-led coalition. The coalition said it intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles fired towards Riyadh early on Saturday. It marks the second Houthi attack on the Saudi capital in recent days, following Saudi-led strikes on Houthi targets in Yemen. Yuka Royer has the latest.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Russian projectiles hit Poland as NATO tensions rise
stories.description: Three Russian projectiles came down in Poland on Friday, prompting NATO to condemn what it called a grave violation of Polish airspace. A suspected jet-powered drone and a missile struck separate locations near the Ukrainian border, while another missile crashed just 35 kilometres from an area where European troops are taking part in military exercises. Meanwhile, troops from eight NATO countries are conducting drills in neighbouring Lithuania. With US-led peace talks yet to make a breakthrough, tensions between Europe and Russia remain high. Peter O’Brien reports.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Nations League: France to face Spain in quarter-finals, England to take on Norway
stories.description: A chance for revenge. Beaten by Spain in the World Cup semi-finals last July, France will meet La Roja again in the Nations League quarter-finals next March.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: EU, UK reach reset deal after Brexit
stories.description: The UK and the EU signed three agreements on Friday at a summit in Brussels, marking a new effort to reset post-Brexit relations. The deals aim to reduce red tape for food exports, link emissions trading schemes and allow tens of thousands of young people to live and work more freely across the Channel. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has called Brexit an “obvious failure” to deliver on its promises and wants to deepen ties with the EU, a position criticised by veteran Brexiteer Nigel Farage, who has warned of a political backlash. Daniel Quinlan has this story.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Live: France braces for fresh protests as social unrest enters sixth week
stories.description: France is bracing for a sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, with demonstrators expected to rally over the rising cost of living and the government's handling of weeks of social unrest ahead of next year's presidential election. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: US Agriculture Department and FBI hit by cyberattacks, media report
stories.description: Hackers breached systerms at the US Agriculture Department and the FBI, US media reported, amid a recent wave of major technology disruptions across the country.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: House of Cards: America's enemies "no longer fear it, its allies no longer trust it'
stories.description: The Economist's deputy editor Tom Standage joins us for a futuristic retrospective, taking us back to the future as we spotlight "The World Ahead 2027". We begin with the "leader of the free world", the FIFA Peace Prize recipient presiding over an America under the "Donroe Doctrine": "Its enemies no longer fear it and its allies no longer trust it in the way they did before."
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Paris police officers sentenced to prison over 2020 beating of Black man
stories.description: A Paris court on Friday sentenced three policemen to serve time over the 2020 beating of Black music producer Michel Zecler, a rare such ruling. The assault, which was captured on camera, sparked nationwide outrage and renewed scrutiny of police violence and racism in France.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Guinea bans Burkina Faso broadcaster, escalating diplomatic tensions
stories.description: Tensions rise between Guinea and Burkina Faso after Conakry bans Burkinabe broadcaster RTB, amid a diplomatic dispute over gold miners and a caricature of President Mamadi Doumbouya. Meanwhile, fighting erupts between Congolese forces and the Rwanda-backed FRN group in eastern DR Congo, despite peace commitments. Finally, in Ethiopia, one entrepreneur is tackling period poverty by breaking menstrual stigma and making reusable sanitary pads more accessible.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'Licence to kill': French parliament adopts police shootings law slammed by activists
stories.description: French senators gave final approval on Friday to controversial legislation granting police officers a presumption of legitimate self-defence when using firearms, fulfilling a long-standing demand of the far right even as weeks of student-led protests have thrust the issue of police brutality back into the spotlight. Left-wing lawmakers have vowed to challenge the bill before France's Constitutional Council.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'Friends' But Who Benefits? Notes from an Historic Summit, Myanmar's Genocide Ruling, Time to 'Bre-join' the EU?
stories.description: Welcome to the World This Week with Gavin Lee. You give us 45 minutes, we'll give you 7 days worth of crystal clear analysis. As ever, alongside a handpicked panel of four distinguished foreign correspondents.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Yemen's Houthis target Riyadh after Saudi coalition's 'special operation'
stories.description: Yemen's Houthi rebels launched strikes on Riyadh on Saturday after Saudi-led coalition air raids on Yemen, escalating a months-long surge in cross-border attacks.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 🦛 USA: Fiona, Cincinnati Zoo’s famous hippo, has died
stories.description: 🦛Fiona, Cincinnati Zoo’s beloved hippo, has died aged just 9, after swallowing a knitted hat that fell into her enclosure. Born prematurely and weighing only 13kg, she captured millions of hearts around the world and became an internet sensation.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: 🔴Watch live: Trump holds press conference after meeting with Xi, Putin
stories.subject: World

stories.title: UK and EU strike ‘landmark’ deal to rebuild ties after Brexit
stories.description: 🇬🇧🇪🇺 A fresh start after #Brexit? The #UK and #EU have agreed on a landmark #deal to rebuild ties, following a summit in Brussels this Friday. The agreement covers easier food export checks, youth mobility and carbon emission quotas.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: A cultural stroll through Paris with singer-songwriters Mariam Doumbia and Zaho
stories.description: Two women, two voices, two destinies: Malian performer Mariam continues her musical journey after the 2025 passing of Amadou, her partner in life and on stage. "Amadou and I sang about love. We wanted to share love with everyone. We sang of peace, of love, of justice."
stories.subject: World

stories.title: ‘A more expensive EU is not a better EU’: Austria's Minister for Europe, Claudia Bauer
stories.description: This week's programme hosted Claudia Bauer, Austria’s Federal Minister for Europe, Integration and Family while she was in Paris for the recent G7 meeting. She offered her thoughts on the diplomatic moves surrounding Ukraine, transatlantic relations, EU enlargement and a headscarf ban in Austrian schools that has caused disquiet. We also talked about the thorny negotiations involved in the EU’s next long-term budget: the Multiannual Financial Framework.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Photography: A very French history
stories.description: From its use as creative expression to documenting our everyday reality, photography has become an essential and widely-accessible medium since its invention. Did you know, however, that the technology was developed in France? FRANCE 24's Tanishk Saha takes a look at the French legacy of photography.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: France investigates actor Depardieu, writer Houellebecq over alleged gang rape
stories.description: French police are investigating allegations actor and convicted sex offender Gérard Depardieu raped and assaulted a woman with the complicity of bestselling author Michel Houellebecq during a 2018 film shoot, two sources following the case said Friday. The plaintiff has accused the film's director Guillaume Nicloux of being complicit in the abuse.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: 'Blade Runner 2099' & 'Rivals': The big TV shows to watch this month
stories.description: "Blade Runner" returns with a futuristic twist, while British bonkbuster "Rivals" is back with part two of season two. TV critic Dheepthika Laurent joins Eve Jackson to review the month’s big releases, including Netflix’s acclaimed Arctic comedy "North of North" and the lavish K-drama "Remarried Empress".
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Gen Z protests spread across Europe: Mass rallies over cost of living in Spain
stories.description: Protesters across Europe are set took to the streets on Friday in a show of cross-border solidarity, joining coordinated demonstrations against the rising cost of living, militarisation and other causes, in a bid to increase pressure on their governments. Protesters across Europe are set to take to the streets on Friday in a show of cross-border solidarity, joining coordinated demonstrations against the rising cost of living, militarisation and other causes, in a bid to increase pressure on their governments. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Madrid, Spain.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: French ex-PM Villepin announces presidential run
stories.description: France's former prime minister and foreign minister Dominique de Villepin, famed abroad for his excoriating 2003 denunciation of US plans for invading Iraq, said on Friday he was running for president. Villepin enters an already crowded field of candidates seeking to succeed President Emmanuel Macron, with polls pointing towards a possible run-off between frontrunner Marine Le Pen of the far-right National Rally (RN) and hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) veteran Jean-Luc Melenchon.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Shenzhen trilateral: Xi Jinping's 'masterclass in diplomatic theatre'
stories.description: Xi Jinping positioned himself as a great statesman when he met with the US president and Russia's Vladimir Putin for trilateral talks in Shenzhen this week. But while the Chinese president sparkled on the world stage, does he have anything to show for it? Seong-Hyon Lee, an associate at Harvard University Asia Center, tells us how the trilateral has come up short on deliverables.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Spain’s political crossroads, Europe’s wider stakes: Spaniards to vote in key election
stories.description: The stakes are high – not only for people in Spain, but also for Europe. On November 29, the country holds a parliamentary election that could see the end of the Socialist-led government and potentially a coalition between the right and the far right, in one of the EU’s biggest and most influential member states. It could also signal the end of Pedro Sanchez’s third term in office. Among other things, the prime minister may pay the political price for two shocking train crashes and the migrant crisis in Spain’s North African exclave of Ceuta.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Jamaica's beaches are increasingly off limits to locals
stories.description: Jamaica usually conjures up images of white sandy beaches, Rastafari culture and Bob Marley – but another reality exists. On this small Caribbean island, less than 1 percent of the coastline is freely accessible to local people. The rest has gradually been privatised, mostly for large hotel developments and private homes.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Cincinnati Zoo's famed Fiona the hippo dies days after eating a visitor’s hat
stories.description: Fiona, the hippo whose premature birth and fight for survival at the Cincinnati Zoo turned her into a global sensation nearly a decade ago, died Thursday from complications after swallowing a knit hat that was accidentally flung into her enclosure. She was 9 years old. “It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency,” the zoo said in a statement.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: REPLAY: Burnham, Von der Leyen hail 'turning point' in EU-UK relations
stories.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham hailed a "landmark" deal with the European Union on Friday, as the two sides sealed pacts on food exports, emissions-trading schemes and youth mobility at a summit in Brussels. EU chief Ursula von der Leyen welcomed a "turning point" in ties with Britain following Brexit. Watch our replay.
stories.subject: Climate

stories.title: COP31 wrapping up in Turkey: Climate deal elusive as fossil fuels go unmentioned
stories.description: The UN's COP31 climate talks were set to spill into overtime Friday as countries remained deadlocked over a draft deal that makes no mention of fossil fuels, with a host of other disputes also snarling negotiations. The talks come with a series of stark reminders of the urgency of climate action, from heatwaves in Europe and devastating floods in Nepal, while a record-breaking El Nino supercharges temperatures. FRANCE 24's Environment Editor Valerie Dekimpe tells us more.
stories.subject: Climate

stories.title: Burnham hails 'landmark' EU-UK deal as 'good day' for Britain, Europe
stories.description: Britain and the European Union agreed deals on trade, carbon emissions and youth movement on Friday, and pledged to rebuild ties with an “ambitious and dynamic” post-Brexit relationship. In a joint statement after a summit in Brussels, the UK and EU confirmed agreements that will scrap checks on the trade in plant and animal products, link their emissions trading schemes and let 100,000 young adults from each side live and work in the other's countries for up to three years. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.
stories.subject: Climate

stories.title: Russia pummels Ukraine with massive strikes, missile hits Poland
stories.description: Moscow pounded Ukraine with massive strikes Friday, with Kyiv saying at least six people were killed in the capital, and neighbouring Poland reporting two Russian missiles likely landed in the south-east corner of the NATO country, accusing Moscow of a "provocation." Hours earlier, Russia's Vladimir Putin vowed a "painful" response to Kyiv's strikes on Moscow's Crimea bridge after holding a summit with China's Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Kyiv, Ukraine.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'GTA VI': When the biggest-ever entertainment release becomes the biggest headline
stories.description: This week FRANCE 24's media show "Scoop" looks at how the press covered the release of "Grand Theft Auto VI". Pre-orders and first-day sales totalled more than $2.3 billion. What does the game and the franchise's success mean for the future of entertainment? Our guest is Margaret Wallace, a video game developer and an associate professor of the practice of media innovation at Boston University.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: France probes suspected leak of confidential information to Le Pen's party
stories.description: French authorities are investigating whether a former senior official at the Interior Ministry leaked confidential information about judicial investigations into far-right leader Marine Le Pen's National Rally, adding to the party's legal woes ahead of a presidential election next year in which Le Pen is the current frontrunner.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: A decade after Brexit, do Britons regret leaving the EU?
stories.description: Britain and the European Union went through a bitter divorce, then slowly began trying to rebuild their relationship. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham met the EU's top officials in Brussels on Friday for a summit he has described as a step towards undoing a decade of damage caused by the 2016 vote to leave the bloc. But how do the British public feel about closer ties with the EU – and, potentially, rejoining it?
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Does staggered consent actually protect young people?
stories.description: Following recent scandals involving two iconic British comedians, the UK government is considering the introduction of staggered age consent. Annette Young talks to Katherine Allen from the Institute of Social Justice and Crime in the UK about whether such laws work. Also the social costs of femicide; how do loved ones cope with such a loss, and what support is available to families in the wake of such a tragedy? Plus we meet the women who are challenging the traditions of Mexican mariachi music, a world that remains largely male dominated.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: El Salvador: Nayib Bukele, self-proclaimed “coolest dictator on earth”, is seeking a third term
stories.description: 🇸🇻 El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele, who calls himself the “coolest dictator on earth”, is seeking a third term after changing the Constitution to scrap presidential term limits. His war on gangs has made him hugely popular, but also sparked serious human rights concerns.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 🔴 France seeks UN Security Council meeting after Russian strikes hit European embassies in Kyiv
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Malaysia's unwanted refugees: The plight of the Rohingya
stories.description: On November 19, the International Court of Justice delivered a historic ruling: finding Myanmar guilty of committing genocide against the Rohingya in 2017. Malaysia has long been a supporter of the persecuted Muslim minority. But its role as a safe haven is coming to an end, amid a rise in hate speech and calls for the expulsion of Rohingya via social media.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Italy strike draws workers, students into nationwide protests over wages and living costs
stories.description: A nationwide strike was expected to disrupt schools, hospitals and local transport across Italy on Friday as workers and students began marching in dozens of cities to demand higher wages, lower living costs and greater social protections. The labor action coincided with an International Day of Student Mobilisation, with organisers planning demonstrations in more than 45 Italian cities. FRANCE 24's Seema Gupta reports from Rome, Italy.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: South Africa: High Court examines asylum seekers' detention at Lindela centre
stories.description: South Africa's High Court judges visited the Lindela Repatriation Centre in Krugersdorp this week, ahead of delivering a ruling on 33 urgent applications concerning the detention of asylum seekers. The court is examining conflicting interpretations of a Constitutional Court ruling that prohibits the deportation of asylum seekers whose claims are still being processed. The case comes amid a wider and increasingly tense debate over immigration in South Africa, which has at times spilled over into deadly xenophobic violence. FRANCE 24's Eunice Masson reports from Cape Town, South Africa.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'Our culture and identity': Deaf Nigerians embrace indigenous sign languages
stories.description: With a quick flick of the wrist, Umaru Zayyanu conveys the phrase "I am a Nigerian". But the 37-year-old is not signing, rather in the west African nation's official sign language. Instead, he's using Hausa sign language. Such indigenous sign languages abound in Africa's most populous country, where deaf people were communicating with each other long before the advent of formal sign language taught in deaf schools, in 1960.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Europe's youth set to join mass cost of living protests in 25 countries
stories.description: Youth protests are set to take place in more than 25 countries in Europe on Friday and over the weekend, coalition organisers said, as demostrators seek to increase pressure on governments over issues including soaring housing costs and deteriorating learning conditions with a show of cross-border solidarity.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: FIFA: Infantino, Tashima and Diallo enter presidential race
stories.description: Three candidates have officially submitted their bids for the FIFA presidency. Gianni Infantino, who has been in office for 11 years, is seeking a fourth consecutive term. Backed by UEFA, French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo wants to offer an alternative to Infantino’s leadership. He will face Japan’s Kohzo Tashima, honorary president of the Japan Football Association. The election will take place on March 18, 2027 in Rabat, Morocco.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Czechs protest en masse against 'concentration of power in one hand' and growing control over media
stories.description: As large demonstrations in the Czech Republic challenge Prime Minister Andrej Babiš's plans to change the funding model of public broadcasters, Mikuláš Minář, Chair of the Million Moments for Democracy movement, joins François Picard from Prague for Spotlight, warning that his country risks following Hungary and Slovakia in democratic backsliding. "We are really afraid that the Czech Republic is following the Orbánian Hungarian way, (Fico's) Slovakian way," he says.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: EU and UK set to sign deals on trade, energy, youth mobility at Brussels summit
stories.description: The UK and the EU are poised to agree new deals on trade, energy and youth mobility at a summit in Brussels on Friday, as part of UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham's bid to reset ties with the bloc. Burnham – who has said he hopes to see Britain rejoin the EU in his lifetime – argues the deals will help fix some of the damage Brexit inflicted.
stories.subject: Business

stories.title: White House fires national cyber director over widespread outages
stories.description: The White House fired national cyber director Sean Cairncross on Thursday following a week of technology disruptions affecting US air travel, email services and national security systems. The departure comes as the Trump administration faces criticism over its response to the outages, which officials say were unrelated incidents.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: PM Sánchez admits 'mistakes' in key debate ahead of Spain's election
stories.description: Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez acknowledged shortcomings in his government on Thursday as he faced conservative rival Alberto Núñez Feijóo in the campaign's only televised debate. The November 29 election could leave the far-right Vox party in a position to enter government.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Voyager 1 spacecraft reaches one light-day milestone
stories.description: NASA's Voyager 1 probe, which has been traveling through space for nearly 50 years, hit a milestone distance of one light-day away from Earth on Wednesday. Already the most distant man-made object in the universe, the spacecraft is now about 26 billion kilometers (16 billion miles) away, according to the US space agency. That is the distance a particle of light can travel in 24 hours. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.
stories.subject: Science

stories.title: Major anti-gang offensive in Haiti kills 34 suspected gang members
stories.description: Haitian security forces launched a major offensive on Thursday to retake Martissant, a strategic corridor linking Port-au-Prince with the country's western and southern regions that gangs have controlled for five years. Police said at least 34 suspected gang members were killed in clashes involving a private security task force.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Anthropic goes public after blockbuster IPO but fails to revive AI trade
stories.description: Anthropic has become the first pure-play AI developer to be publicly traded on the stock market, following a record-setting IPO. The stock opened 34% higher, briefly valuing the company at more than $2 trillion, before ending its first day of trading up 17%. However, Wall Street indexes closed sharply lower as investors took profits, reflecting underlying market jitters about the AI trade.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: French far-left candidate Mélenchon opens door to alliance with rival Greens candidate
stories.description: French far-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon opened the door to an alliance with France's Greens on Thursday after their presidential candidate Marine Tondelier said she was ready to "work on a coalition around" the veteran leftist. Tondelier's overture has further boosted Mélenchon's campaign for the Élysée Palace – and angered moderates on the centre-left.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Kenyan marathon champion banned for doping
stories.description: In tonight's edition, Kenyan athletics superstar and reigning marathon world champion Peres Jepchirchir is banned for three years for doping. Also, South African judges leave the courtroom behind and tour a repatriation centre before handing down judgment in 33 emergency asylum applications. And Ghana's presidency has a new jet, but critics of the ruling party are not on board.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Russian strikes on Kyiv kill one, damage Dutch and Austrian embassies
stories.description: A wave of daytime Russian strikes on Kyiv on Thursday killed one person and damaged a historic cathedral as well as the embassies of Austria and the Netherlands. Loud explosions erupted across the Ukraine capital throughout the day as the leaders of Russia, China and the United States held a historic meeting in China that put Russia's President Vladimir Putin in international spotlight. FRANCE 24's Laurent Berstecher reports.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'We're seeing in real time the effects that AI is going to have on cybersecurity', expert says
stories.description: FRANCE 24's Monte Francis speaks with Dr. R. David Edelman, Senior Fellow at the Brookings Institution, also former Director for Cybersecurity on the National Security Council under the Obama administration. He explains that the latest spate of network outages shows "in real time the effects that AI is going to have on cybersecurity" adding that "the one thing that's tying most of these outages together is that companies and institutions are racing to patch a system that's been identified as vulnerable, and they're patching what themselves are pretty creaky digital systems".
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Kushner says Trump 'open' to extend NATO mutual defense-type clause to Ukraine
stories.description: US envoy Jared Kushner said Thursday that President Donald Trump was open to extending to Ukraine a security guarantee similar to NATO's mutual defense clause, but stressed that Washington has to protect its interests too. The comments came as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz qualified the summit between the presidents of the United States, Russia and China as a "photo op". FRANCE 24's international affairs commentator Douglas Herbert explains.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Macron urges Ukraine's allies to 'reopen the question' of NATO membership
stories.description: French President Emmanuel Macron on Thursday called for Ukraine's allies to speed up the delivery of urgently needed air defence systems and urged them to "reopen the question" of Ukraine's NATO membership after talks in Berlin aimed at reaffirming European support for Kyiv.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: A president among body bags: Photo ops spark outrage in Colombia
stories.description: Since taking office in August, Colombia's far-right President Abelardo de la Espriella has regularly posted videos that show him walking among body bags supposedly holding the remains of rebel fighters – a communications strategy that has sparked widespread criticism.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Three of a kind? Xi hosts Trump and Putin as Ukraine war grinds on
stories.description: Gang of three or glorified photo op? Xi Jinping hosting Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the APEC summit. Already, our Monday panel rejected attempts to paint the three-way meeting as a new Yalta, as in the 1945 sit-down on the Black Sea that defined the post-war security architecture of Europe.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral meeting: Trump's recognition of China and Russia as 'peers of the US'
stories.description: Genie Godula is pleased to welcome Olivia Cheung. The trilateral meeting between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit was significant despite the absence of concrete agreements, according to Cheung. “The significance is seen in the precedence of the United States seeing and giving recognition that China and Russia are peers of the United States,” she explained, adding that “the image of a G3 is very significant.”
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: NASA's Voyager 1 phones home from record one light-day away, 49 years after launch
stories.description: The Voyager 1 probe launched by NASA nearly a half century ago has reached a distance from Earth of one light day (more than 26 billion kilometres), the farthest any human artifact has ever ventured from our planet. The space agency received a signal from the spacecraft Thursday, exactly 24 hours after it was sent.
stories.subject: Science

stories.title: French media regulator says it will monitor top YouTubers for bias in election coverage
stories.description: Rules designed to safeguard media pluralism during elections campaigns will apply to France's most influential YouTubers in the run-up to next year's presidential contest, media regulator Arcom warned on Thursday, reflecting the growing influence of content creators whose audiences often outstrip those of traditional media companies.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: What impact will the Shenzhen summit have on the US-China trade war?
stories.description: Despite warm words between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at three-way talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen Thursday, the simmering trade war between Washington and Beijing still looks to be no closer to resolution.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Bangladesh: Hasina supporters vandalise ruling party office
stories.description: Hundreds of supporters of ousted Bangladesh premier Sheikh Hasina staged street protests on Thursday, as a wave of arson attacks escalated tensions ahead of her planned return from exile next month.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: US has 'unbalanced approach' on DR Congo deal, Rwanda's foreign minister says
stories.description: In an interview with FRANCE 24, Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe said the Trump administration had "an unbalanced approach" in implementing the DR Congo peace deal it brokered. He also said that the recent row over the Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie's top job was "manufactured in Paris and Kinshasa". Finally, he defended a deal for Rwanda to host failed asylum seekers from five European countries.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: 🔴Anthropic soars more than 30% to $2 trillion valuation on first day of trading
stories.subject: World

stories.title: How much do businesses want to pay for AI?
stories.description: Four years after ChatGPT went mainstream, generative AI is transforming how we live and work. It's also been a major driver of economic growth, with massive amounts of money poured into expanding global computing capacity. But now, there are signs of a slowdown in AI spending as companies take a reality check: are they getting sufficient returns on their investments and how much artificial intelligence do they actually need?
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Inside France's mental health crisis: Are the French all right?
stories.description: This week, we try to get inside the heads of French people, with a deep dive into mental health in France. For a nation that loves analysing its problems, its mental health figures make for sobering reading: nearly one in five French people are affected by a mental health issue.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: ICJ ruling on Myanmar genocide: ‘Historic victory for Rohingya, landmark for international justice’
stories.description: Erin Ogunkeye welcomes Reed Brody, Member of the International Commission of Jurists, Human Rights Lawyer and veteran war crimes prosecutor. The International Court of Justice's ruling on Myanmar marks, according to Brody, "a historic victory for the Rohingya, but also a landmark for international justice." He explains how the court assessed evidence of genocidal intent, rejecting Myanmar's justification of its military operations as counterterrorism. He argues that "the existence of an armed conflict or a security objective doesn't exclude genocidal intent," a finding he believes will have "far-reaching implications in future genocide cases," including South Africa's case against Israel over Gaza. Brody also discusses the Gambia's role in bringing the case and growing challenges to international accountability, warning that "we're in a very dangerous moment."
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Xi demonstrating China's 'global status', occupying 'central position' in relation to Trump & Putin
stories.description: Sharon Gaffney is pleased to welcome Rex Li, professor of international relations at King's College London. For Professor Li, the meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in China is less about "reaching concrete agreements and a common position." Rather, he argues, it is about demonstrating Xi's ability to bring the American and Russian leaders together to discuss major geopolitical issues. Li believes that Xi Jinping has the most to gain from the meeting, as it allows him to demonstrate China's global status and its role as a diplomatic convener. Putin may also benefit from the opportunity to meet the two leaders despite Russia's international isolation following its invasion of Ukraine.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Gender pay gap: French women work "for free” from today
stories.description: Women in Europe are still paid less than men, with the gap falling from 15.1% in 2016 to 11.1% in 2024, according to Eurostat. In France, women symbolically start working for free from 10:51 am on Thursday, 19 November, and at the current pace equality would not be reached until 2062. Experts warn that AI could make things worse by eliminating administrative and legal jobs where many women work, while childbirth and short paternity leave continue to slow women’s careers.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'GTA VI': A masterpiece? Fans react to gaming's biggest release
stories.description: Critics are calling the new "Grand Theft Auto VI" a masterpiece. In this edition of arts24, we hear what fans make of one of the biggest video game releases in history. We also look at U2's new album and tour marking 50 years of the band, discover the French comic book that Pope Leo is reading and meet the women redefining Mexico's Mariachi tradition.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: The chocolate countdown: The art of the advent calendar
stories.description: The holiday season is almost upon us and with it come advent calendars. The annual physical countdown originated in 19th-century Germany as a Christian tradition to count down the days until Christmas. Eugénie Pont from the magazine Fou de Pâtisserie tells us more about what we can expect from the biggest chocolate makers in France.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Trump, Xi, Putin summit: What was it all about?
stories.description: Donald Trump has left China after a historic first meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the APEC summit. Ukraine was discussed without Kyiv or European leaders in the room, which raised eyebrows, though Trump defended dialogue with rivals and Putin said the talks created conditions for future agreements. Xi warned major powers against conflict, and topics included reducing nuclear risks, reforming the UN and increasing energy flows.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Behind the UK's use of AI in asylum applications
stories.description: The UK is increasingly turning to artificial intelligence to manage its immigration system, from analysing migrants’ phones to processing asylum applications. But what happens when AI gets involved in deciding how an asylum seeker's story is understood? Stella Elgersma, journalist at InfoMigrants, explains how the UK Home Office is testing AI tools to process asylum applications, including a system that generates summaries of asylum interviews. With errors, limited human oversight and concerns over transparency, could AI put asylum seekers’ lives at risk?
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Haiti: Salvador’s Bukele publishes video of attack on gang leader’s house
stories.description: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele said Wednesday that his troops demolished the lavish home of a prominent gang leader in Haiti known as Jeff Gwo Lwa. "My gift to the Haitian people on the anniversary of the Battle of Vertières," Bukele wrote on X - referencing a 1803 battle critical in helping secure Haiti's independence from France.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Beaujolais Nouveau: A French tradition uncorked
stories.description: Every year on the third Thursday of November, France raises a glass to one of its most joyful traditions: Le Beaujolais Nouveau! That means that this Thursday, millions of bottles of the 2026 young red wine will be uncorked around the world, from Lyon to New York. Olivier Badoureaux, wine expert and director of the French trade organisation Inter Beaujolais, tells us what we should expect from this year's vintage.
stories.subject: Business

stories.title: France: Retirees march against 2027 budget cuts
stories.description: More than a thousand people marched in Paris on Thursday, called by a union alliance joined by student and high-school groups, to protest social and tax measures targeting retirees in the 2027 budgets. The government wants retirees to contribute about €5.4 billion, by freezing the indexation of pensions above €1,260 and reforming their 10% income tax allowance. Union leaders say the money should not come from retirees’ pockets, as FRANCE 24's Luke Shrago explains.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Chef Rachel Khoo: 'You don't need fancy kitchen gadgets to cook delicious food'
stories.description: One of the world's best-known chefs has spoken to FRANCE 24 about her new book that proves you certainly don't need fancy kitchen gadgets to cook delicious meals. The book "The Smallest Restaurant in Paris" tells her own story of starting out in a tiny Parisian flat cooking food just for two people at a time. That then led to a BBC series and a decade of writing and filming cooking stories. Rachel Khoo is now a judge on "The Great Australian Bake Off". She spoke to us in Perspective.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: ICJ rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
stories.description: In August 2017, after attacks by a Rohingya militia, Myanmar’s army launched a “clearance campaign” in Rakhine state, with survivors describing mass killings, rapes and burned villages as hundreds of thousands fled to Bangladesh. The Gambia took Myanmar to the ICJ in 2019, and after a seven-year legal fight the court has ruled that Myanmar committed acts of genocide. Meanwhile some 1.2 million Rohingya remain in crowded camps, unable to return home.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: China summit ends with little new, Europe backs Ukraine in Berlin
stories.description: The leaders of China, the United States and Russia met in Shenzhen for a historic first, but the summit brought little new: non-binding statements on peace and no plan to meet regularly. In Berlin, Europeans gathered to show their support for Ukraine, a pointed answer to a summit where Europe had no seat, as FRANCE 24's Kethevane Gorjestani explains.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: In South Korea, women forced into prostitution on US military bases seek justice
stories.description: Tens of thousands of women were forced to work in South Korean state-sanctioned brothels used by American soldiers based in the country after the Korean War. They were raped, physically abused and forcibly confined. Now, after decades of silence, some of these women are speaking out.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'Their lives, their rights, their history': Not the end of accountability for the Rohingya people'
stories.description: Oliver Farry welcomes Sonya Sceats, Director and CEO of the British Institute of International and Comparative Law. The case brought by The Gambia against Myanmar before the ICJ, and the court ruling, both have great significance for the Rohingya people, the interpretation of the Genocide Convention and the possibility of future criminal proceedings. The case could also have important implications for South Africa's proceedings against Israel, where there are “many similarities between the two cases.”
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 24-month matured Comté crowned world’s best cheese
stories.description: With its nutty flavour and smooth, supple texture, it was aged for two years in a former military fortress in eastern France. Comté, an unpasteurised cow’s milk cheese from the Jura Mountains, has beaten more than five thousand challengers to the top prize at the prestigious annual 'World Cheese Awards'. FRANCE 24's Daniel Whittington has the story.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Inside Limoges City Hall devastated by arson attack
stories.description: Work is underway to restore the city hall of Limoges, in central France, which was devastated by an arson attack during riots on October 17. More than €1.7 million has been raised through an online fundraising campaign in the wake of the disaster. Also on the show, the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI has finally been released, with gamers in Oceania among the first to get a taste of the latest instalment in the video game franchise.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Crimea bridge strike: Fact-checking fake videos of damage after Ukraine's attack
stories.description: Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, but not all the dramatic footage circulating online is real. Multiple AI-generated videos falsely show the bridge collapsed with extensive damage. Some even used branding resembling a Ukrainian news agency to appear credible. While the bridge was indeed struck and damaged, the viral videos were fabricated using AI, as Vedika Bahl explains.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Bassirou Diomaye Faye excluded from Senegal's ruling party
stories.description: In tonight's edition, the political divorce between Senegal's president and the powerful former prime minister and mentor is official. Also, all of Nigeria's states have shown willingness for a push to create their own police forces. And in parts of the continent, conflict and a drop in funding have placed huge pressures on children's learning.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Reconstruction begins at Limoges City Hall after devastating fire
stories.description: It's been a month since the nationwide protests that degenerated in violence across France. The dramatic pictures of the historic City Hall in the French city of Limoges set on fire made headlines worldwide. To the relief of many, the reconstruction work on the building has now begun. Since the fire, donations have poured in and already about 80 percent of the necessary funding has been secured. FRANCE 24's Caitlin Brown reports.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: US Democrats nominate Jeffries to be first Black House speaker
stories.description: Hakeem Jeffries is on the cusp of becoming the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives after Democrats elected him their leader Wednesday following a sweeping midterm election triumph. Jeffries faced no declared challenger, although opposition from some newly elected progressives had exposed divisions over how Democrats should wield their newfound power. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson reports from Washington.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Israeli army launches ground operation in Hamas-controlled area of Gaza
stories.description: The Israeli military said it had launched an operation on Wednesday in a Hamas-controlled area of central Gaza, where an AFP journalist saw Israeli tanks position themselves east of the Nuseirat refugee camp. The rare ground operation comes after inconclusive Israeli elections, with the opposition's Gadi Eisenkot trying to form a government without caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has built his brand on saying he will ensure Israel's security. FRANCE 24's Daniel Whittington reports.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'Netanyahu's only 2 tickets are racism or starting a war: He stopped acting as a democratic player'
stories.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Israeli writer and filmmaker Etgar Keret, author of "The Seven Good Years", joining us from Tel Aviv. Keret argues that Netanyahu is seeking to remain in power, at any cost, including delegitimizing Arab parties and prolonging conflict. “For him, it could be a never-ending war as long as he's in power. He has no incentive to stop it,” he warns. Keret also calls for Israelis to examine how the war in Gaza was conducted, arguing that “the media as a whole ignored the war.”
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Xi welcomes Trump: Does Nvidia scandal upend US-China AI race?
stories.description: You can strike Jensen Huang from the guest list but good luck steering dinner conversation away from the topic in Shenzhen. The co-founder of the AI computing leader was to accompany the US president to the APEC summit before he was undone by revelations of a dalliance with a Chinese national that happened to coincide with a Singapore client's backdoor skirting of sanctions on its powerful H200 chips.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Hegseth makes surprise trip to Venezuela, renews military cooperation
stories.description: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unannounced visit to Caracas on Wednesday, announcing a resumption of military cooperation with Venezuela and vowing to crack down on drug traffickers. The trip marks the highest-level US visit since the ouster of Nicolas Maduro in January, signalling a dramatic shift in relations between the two countries.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Why Ukraine keeps trying to bring down Russia's bridge to Crimea
stories.description: A Ukrainian drone and missile strike on Monday night brought down a stretch of the bridge linking the annexed Crimean Peninsula to Russia, potentially crippling a route long used by Moscow to move men and materiel into Crimea and the southern front. Here’s why Kyiv keeps testing its strength against an infrastructure project that has become synonymous with Russian President Vladimir Putin’s 2014 seizure of the peninsula.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Beijing has supported Moscow but 'China understands that America is way more important than Russia'
stories.description: Following Xi Jinping's very friendly rare tarmac greeting for Donald Trump, Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Kerry Brown, Professor of Chinese Studies and Director of the Lau China Institute at King's College, London. Brown examines the complex relationship between the world's two largest economies, China's growing diplomatic influence and the competition over artificial intelligence.“China is the diplomatic center of the world,” says Brown, pointing to Beijing's ability to bring together leaders from Russia, the United States, Europe and elsewhere. He argues that China now has “extraordinary convening power" and significant influence over Russia.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: French ex-PM Philippe pledges to slash spending, hike retirement age as Elysée bid falters
stories.description: Former prime minister Édouard Philippe pledged on Wednesday to slash public spending, scrap France’s statutory 35-hour workweek and raise the retirement age to 65 from the current 62.9 years as he unveiled a slew of measures aimed a staving off economic "catastrophe" for France. An early frontrunner in next year's presidential election, Philippe is now trailing rivals in opinion polls and at risk of missing out on the second-round runoff.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: War in Ukraine: Is France in direct conflict with Russia?
stories.description: An investigation published by the French public radio channel RFI on November 17 revealed that a confidential mission by the French army known as "Volia" has been used for months to conceal the presence of French personnel in Ukraine. Russia was prompt to accuse France of direct involvement in the conflict. Is this true?
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Senate leadership challenge exposes divisions among Democrat
stories.description: As Democrats prepare to take control of the Senate, incumbent minority leader Chuck Schumer is facing an insurgent leadership bid from Senator Chris Van Hollen and disputes over party leadership are exposing divisions over what direction to take the Democratic party after their midterms sweep.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Russia’s new low-cost munitions pose a fresh threat to Ukraine
stories.description: Dan-T, Filin and Geran-5 might not mean anything to you, but in Ukraine, everyone is talking about these munitions. These new Russian weapons are small, fast and cheap – and a major threat, as they were specially designed to get around Ukrainian anti-aircraft defences and strike deep within the country.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Israel begins new military operation in Gaza
stories.description: Israeli tanks advanced in an area of the central Gaza Strip on Wednesday, witnesses said, and the Israeli military said its ​forces were targeting ‌Hamas infrastructure outside the "Yellow Line" that sets the boundary of the part of the enclave controlled by Israel "The IDF launched a precise operation within the Gaza Strip earlier today west of the Yellow Line... to remove a threat posed to IDF troops operating in the Gaza Strip," the military said.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Gazans flee shelters as Israeli army launches ground operation beyond Yellow Line
stories.description: Palestinians fled their tents and shelters in central Gaza on Wednesday after Israel launched a rare ground operation in an area it withdrew ​from under a ‌2025 ceasefire. The Israeli army said it crossed the Yellow Line separating Israeli and Hamas-controlled areas "to remove a threat posed to IDF troops operating in the Gaza Strip".
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Yemen: Why the Houthis may besiege Aden rather than storm it
stories.description: Bolstered by their recent military successes, Houthi rebels this week advanced close to the southern port city of Aden, the interim capital of the internationally recognised Yemeni government. Amid territorial ambitions, regional rivalries, and divisions within government forces, the potential fall of this stronghold could permanently alter the balance of power in the country.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 🔴 US Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to be first Black speaker of the House
stories.subject: World

stories.title: French presidential elections 2027: More candidates, more confusion (Episode 2)
stories.description: France will head to the polls to vote for its next president in the spring of 2027. Thirty-eight candidates are currently vying to make it onto the final ballot and have until March 12 to gather backing from 500 elected officials. One figure currently stands out: Marine Le Pen. The far-right National Rally leader has a significant lead in the latest polls.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: WHO sounds alarm over antibiotic resistance
stories.description: The World Health Organization sounded the alarm Monday over antimicrobial resistance, saying the world is off pace to meet key 2030 targets. Many countries have long neglected funding to track and detect dangerous microbes that resist antibiotic treatment, according to a report by the body.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: Xi embraces Trump in China: 'Diplomacy playing out in real time'
stories.description: President Xi Jinping personally greeted US counterpart Donald Trump on the tarmac at a Chinese airport on Wednesday, with the two leaders briefly hugging ahead of their highly anticipated meeting with Russia's Vladimir Putin. Reporting from Shenzhen, France 24's Jan Camenzind Broomby says the warm greeting was a "big sign of respect" from Xi but also a calculated component of diplomatic efforts.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Xi welcomes Trump to China ahead of high-stakes Putin meeting
stories.description: President Xi Jinping personally greeted US counterpart Donald Trump on the tarmac at a Chinese airport on Wednesday, with the two leaders briefly hugging ahead of their highly anticipated meeting with Russia's Vladimir Putin. Beijing has indicated the war in Ukraine will not be discussed during the trilateral meeting, but Trump had said the conflict would find its way onto the agenda, something that experts say is likely to please Putin.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Three leaders, three agendas: Who wants what from Xi-Trump-Putin summit?
stories.description: Be it curbing arms sales to Taiwan, bouncing back after a midterms shellacking, or the optics of a place at the table with the world's two superpowers, Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin are approaching their trilateral meeting in Shenzhen with starkly different aims and agendas. Here's a look at what the Chinese, US and Russian leaders are hoping for.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: US strikes Iranian island after Tehran targets Bahrain
stories.description: The US and Iran exchanged fire on Tuesday, with the US striking an Iranian missile launch site after Iran said it targeted a US military radar system in Bahrain, despite talks between Iran and mediators Oman and Qatar.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Why are measles cases soaring in the US?
stories.description: The United States has lost its long-held status of having eradicated measles as cases of the dangerous and highly contagious virus soar around the country. It follows accusations by medical experts that US President Donald Trump and his health secretary, noted vaccine skeptic Robert F. Kennedy Jr, have fanned distrust in vaccinations, leading to an decline on the number of children getting inoculated against the disease.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond: The surprise casting choice explained
stories.description: Robert Pattinson will be the new James Bond, taking over from Daniel Craig in one of cinema’s most iconic roles.
