Film critic Emma Jones joins Eve Jackson on the arts24 weekly film show to discuss the surprise choice, Pattinson's star power and what he could bring to 007. Plus, they review the latest "Hunger Games" prequel "Sunrise on the Reaping", Lukas Dhont's Cannes prize winner "Coward" and Germany's Oscar entry "Everytime".
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: The calisson: A sweet taste of France's Provence region
stories.description: If you've ever visited the south of France, you may have come across a calisson. These traditional yellow and white almond-shaped candies are everywhere in the region. We tell you all about them with our guest Alexis Bertucat, head of communication and tourism for renowned calisson maker Confiserie du Roy René.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Democrat Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate race in historic victory
stories.description: Democrat Mary Peltola won Alaska's US Senate race on Tuesday, projections from US media showed, defeating Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan and becoming the first Democrat to win a US ‌Senate seat in the state in nearly 20 years and the first Alaska Native ever to do so.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: 'A not so veiled criticism of the US' as Xi blasts protectionism at APEC summit
stories.description: China's President Xi Jinping on Wednesday pledged to stand up against trade protectionism and said regional economies needed to stand up to rising unilateralism in what France 24's Kethevane Gorjestani says was a "a not so veiled criticism of the US". Xi's comments came APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, where a highly anticipated trilateral meeting between Xi, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin is set to take place on Thursday.
stories.subject: Business

stories.title: North Korea completes external works on enrichment facility extension, says IAEA
stories.description: A new extension to North Korea's Yongbyon enrichment facility has been "externally complete" since mid-October, according to the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), which relies on satellite imagery and open sources to monitor the country's nuclear programme. IAEA chief Rafael Grossi on Wednesday said expansion of Pyongyang's enrichment programme remains "cause for serious concern".
stories.subject: World

stories.title: 'Extreme wealth can become a type of brain damage': Journalist Alexander Hurst
stories.description: An international journalist who poured his meagre savings into highly risky options trading at the start of the Covid-19 pandemic and quickly made $1.2 million, before losing it all again, has spoken to FRANCE 24 about his experience. Alexander Hurst works for a number of media outlets, including the Guardian as a correspondent based in Paris.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: 'Failures, incompetence, broken promises': Deutsche Bank exposed in major leak
stories.description: PRESS REVIEW – Wednesday, November 18: A joint investigation following the leak of 15 million documents shows that Deutsche Bank turned a blind eye to the criminal activities of some of its clients. Next, for its 175th birthday, The New York Times has chosen the top 10 stories that made history. Wired is focusing on the moments that defined 2026. Finally, we bring you a story about American parents whose children dream of becoming Formula 1 drivers. But how much does that dream cost?
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Russia, China look to deepen ties at APEC as Trump arrives
stories.description: China's leader Xi Jinping urged closer political and military ties between his country and Russia, as he met with President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on Wednesday on the sidelines of the APEC summit. It comes as Donald Trump arrives in China for trilateral talks with Xi and Putin.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Turkish pro-opposition broadcaster taken off air after police raid
stories.description: Turkish authorities took pro-opposition Sozcu TV off air in a pre-dawn raid on Tuesday and appointed a trustee to run the channel and its website, prosecutors said, extending a crackdown on the opposition and renewing concerns about media freedom.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: US loses measles-free status as cases soar
stories.description: The United States lost its hard-fought measles elimination status after 26 years, the Pan American Health Organization said on Tuesday, as the country failed to curb the continuous spread of the highly contagious virus for more than a year. Bolivia and Mexico have also lost their measles elimination status, the Americas arm of the World Health Organization said.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: Banks, flights, email… What’s behind series of US tech outages?
stories.description: US Secretary of State Marco insisted Wednesday that authorities have found "zero evidence" that recent outages across tech platforms are related to one another or due to the work of "nefarious actors." It follows multiple disruptions of everything from US air traffic operations to Microsoft email and messaging to banking and mobile pay. France 24’s Philip Turle takes a closer look.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Evacuations on the rise in eastern Ukraine as fighting intensifies
stories.description: Civilian evacuations are stepping up in eastern Ukraine as fighting intensifies in the Donetsk region. According to figures released by Ukrainian authorities, more than 6,300 residents left the region in the first ten days of November. . In neighbouring Kharkiv region, hundreds of evacuees arrive every day in the city Lozova, many of whom have lost everything.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: US hits out at Ukraine's 'deep strikes' against Russia in rift with EU over war tactics
stories.description: Top US defence official Elbridge Colby criticised Ukraine's "deep strikes" against Russia Tuesday, as President Volodymyr Zelensky urged Kyiv's backers to send air defences without delay. His comments, delivered at a gathering of Ukraine's allies in Brussels, was flat out rejected by both Germany and the United Kingdom, who hit back at the Americans' suggestion.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: EU proposes new €45 billion Ukraine loan to be repaid by Russia
stories.description: European Commission President Ursula von ⁠der Leyen announced on Wednesday a proposed €45 billion loan to Ukraine for 2027 to help cover around two-thirds ​of Kyiv's financing ​needs. The loan will be repaid ⁠through future ⁠war reparations by Russia, von der Leyen added.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Nvidia posts blockbuster quarterly results amid leadership crisis
stories.description: AI chipmaker Nvidia posted Q3 revenues double those of last year and 20 percent higher than last quarter, while the company board says it has no intention of reinstating disgraced former CEO Jensen Huang. Also in this edition: gaming tourists flock to Miami amid a marketing blitz for the upcoming release of the latest edition in the "Grand Theft Auto" franchise.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Trump says ‘taking seriously’ reports Iran planning Washington dirty-bomb attack
stories.description: President Donald Trump said on Tuesday the US was taking seriously the possibility that Iran could be planning an attack involving a so-called dirty bomb in Washington, after ‌being asked about a CNN ⁠report citing US intelligence assessments. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson denied the allegations in a post on X on Tuesday, calling them "baseless."
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'All eyes on talks with Putin, Xi' as Trump arrives at APEC summit
stories.description: US President Donald Trump arrived in China on Wednesday where the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit is taking place. However, all eyes will be on a historic trilateral meeting between Trump Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin on Thursday. Trump has said that the talks would cover the wars in Iran and Ukraine as well as nuclear disarmament.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 🔴Trump arrives in China ahead of historic three-way summit with Putin, Xi
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Italy approves anti-semitism law despite concerns over freedom of expression
stories.description: Italy's ​parliament on Tuesday approved a new bill aimed at combating anti-semitism – which lists some forms of criticism of ⁠Israel as examples of anti-semitic conduct – despite concerns that it could limit freedom of expression and advocacy for Palestinian rights. The law will not impose financial ⁠penalties or criminal sanctions for offenders.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: AFCON 2027 qualifiers: Senegal and five other nations secure spot
stories.description: The first teams to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations have been decided. Senegal, Cameroon and Morocco are among them.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Peltola defeats Sullivan in Alaska Senate race, expanding Democratic majority
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Xi Jinping calls for global cooperation on AI and free trade at APEC summit
stories.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping called on Wednesday for stronger global cooperation on artificial intelligence and free trade, as he opened the APEC summit in Shenzhen ahead of an expected meeting with US President Donald Trump. Trade tensions and new US chip export restrictions are set to feature prominently.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: 'Taylor Swift of games': Grand Theft Auto is back after 13-year wait
stories.description: "Grand Theft Auto" will be available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles on Thursday after 13 years of waiting, two delays and several leaks. The global gaming phenomenon – dubbed the "Taylor Swift of games" – is the most expensive video game ever developed, and it is on track to break sales records.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Haitians rally behind Bukele as Salvadoran troops battle gangs
stories.description: Thousands of Haitians took to the streets on Tuesday to urge El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele to keep fighting gangs, as his troops bolster security forces in the Caribbean nation. But experts warn that growing public support could turn to anger without a long-term plan to tackle violence and strengthen Haiti's police.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Middle East live: Kuwait, Bahrain report drone and missile attacks
stories.description: Kuwait said Wednesday it was countering hostile drone attacks, while Bahrain reported intercepting Iranian strikes, as US allies in the Gulf remained on alert following an American attack on Iran's Qeshm Island. The incidents came amid a standoff over the Strait of Hormuz. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Nvidia board rules that co-founder Jensen Huang will not return as CEO
stories.description: Nvidia's board chairman ruled out bringing back co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO on Tuesday, as the chipmaker forecast stronger-than-expected quarterly sales but faced growing questions over its leadership, national security exposure and long-term strategy following his abrupt departure.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: WHO sounds the alarm on antimicrobial resistance threat
stories.description: The spread of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is threatening modern medicine despite progress in combating drug-resistant bacteria, senior World Health Organization officials said Monday. WHO officials said countries had expanded efforts to tackle AMR, but warned that progress in prevention, diagnosis and the appropriate use of antibiotics remained too slow to meet global targets. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Jean Pierre Nyemazi, Acting Director of the WHO's AMR Department.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: WHO sounds the alarm on antimicrobial resistance threat
stories.description: The spread of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is threatening modern medicine despite progress in combating drug-resistant bacteria, senior World Health Organization officials said Monday. WHO officials said countries had expanded efforts to tackle AMR, but warned that progress in prevention, diagnosis and the appropriate use of antibiotics remained too slow to meet global targets. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Jean Pierre Nyemazi, Acting Director of the WHO's AMR Department.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: US, Mexico and Bolivia lose measles-free status as deaths mount
stories.description: The US has lost its measles-free status, international health officials said Tuesday, as the highly contagious virus has spread at the fastest rate in more than 30 years, while Mexico and Bolivia also lost their measles-elimination status. Vaccination rates have been falling against a number of diseases, in the US and globally, and measles has been spreading throughout the Americas since 2024.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: 🔴Israeli parliament elects Eisenkot ally Matan Kahana as new Knesset speaker
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: AI imagery complicates Nigeria's election prep
stories.description: In tonight's edition, concerns emerge that AI has been used to generate fake voting profiles ahead of Nigeria's high-stakes general election in January. Also, Nigeria's mining marshal heads underground to unearth some of the people and organizations behind the vast illegal mining industries. And a groundbreaking archaeological discovery in northern Sudan could be the ancient site of the largest church ever built in one of medieval Nubia's most important Christian sites.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Major setbacks for Netanyahu ahead of vote to name new Knesset speaker
stories.description: Since suffering heavy losses in Israel’s Oct. 27 election, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's party has repeatedly claimed the vote was “stolen” by Arab-led parties, possibly with foreign assistance. Those claims appear to be crumbling as he tries to cling to power, as the Israeli parliament is set to select a new speaker opposed to him. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Jensen Huang says he'd be honoured to return to Nvidia as CEO
stories.description: Jensen Huang makes his first public statement since resigning from Nvidia, saying he'd be honoured to return to his job amid support from the tech world. It comes ahead of a much anticipated earnings call this Tuesday, with analysts expecting the group to report a 90% jump in revenue to about $109 billion.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang: Targeted by the AI misinformation he helped create
stories.description: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang has become the target of a wave of AI-generated misinformation, in a striking twist for one of the men behind the AI revolution. From a fake audio recording supposedly featuring his wife to fabricated LinkedIn profiles, false claims linking him to the Chinese Communist Party and viral AI memes, Vedika Bahl examines how deepfakes and misinformation are turning against the former tech boss in Truth or Fake.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Iran 'playing mind games with the United States', expert says
stories.description: President Donald Trump said Tuesday that US authorities take "very seriously" any possible threat to Washington, following reports Iran was planning to target officials, possibly with a radioactive bomb. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Monte Francis, Barbara Slavin, Distinguished Fellow at the Stimson Center in Washington, says that Iran may be "playing mind games with the United States as a way perhaps of deterring President Trump from unleashing a massive new attack on Iran".
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Authorities take over Turkey's last pro-opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV
stories.description: Police raided the Istanbul headquarters of Sozcu TV on Tuesday, dealing another significant blow to Turkey's pro-opposition media. This is the third such seizure of pro-opposition media in just over a year. It comes amid public uproar over a multi-billion investment fund scandal that has affected the savings of nearly half a million people and piled pressure on President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's ruling AKP party ahead of elections in 2028. FRANCE 24's Jasper Mortimer reports from Ankara.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: The centre cannot hold? Splintered moderates lag in French presidential race
stories.description: Five months to go before the French vote in the presidential election first round to choose Emmanuel Macron’s successor. Not much of a race so far for the top two spots and the May Second runoff: there’s the far-right’s Marine Le Pen, the far-left’s Jean-Luc Mélenchon and way behind there’s the rest. Whether on social media or in the streets, their supporters rule. A radical break with the mainstream.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: France: Protesters march for better salaries across the country
stories.description: Tens of thousands of people took part in protests across France on Tuesday after unions called a new nationwide public sector strike to demand pay rises. What started over two months ago as high school student protests has now morphed into a wider movement against the increasing cost of living.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'A lot of anger and a weak government': Why are French public sector workers striking?
stories.description: Tens of thousands of people took part in protests across France on Tuesday after unions called a new nationwide public sector strike to demand pay rises. It follows more than a month of unrest and often violent protests led by students that the government has failed to quell. France 24's Marc Perelman explains.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Deutsche Bank leaks: German lender's dealings with Russian oligarchs under scrutiny
stories.description: Germany's finance minister Tuesday urged "full transparency" from Deutsche Bank after international media outlets published reports based on millions of leaked documents that shine a light on questionable past business practices at the banking giant. They include ties to Russian oligarchs, the convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, and Donald Trump before he became US president. France 24's Douglas Herbert takes a closer look.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Latest cost-of-living protests bring more than 140,000 onto the streets across France
stories.description: Tens of thousands of people took part in protests across France on Tuesday after unions called a new nationwide public sector strike to demand pay rises. Participation was lower compared to previous demonstrations, with 146,000 people demonstrating across the country, according to the interior ministry, compared with 575,000 for the previous unified protests. Unions put Tuesday's number at 550,000.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Organisers hoping for 'joyful' demonstration as French public workers strike
stories.description: France braced for another day of protests Tuesday as unions called for a nationwide strike by public sector workers in a bid to secure pay rises. Hoping to avoid the violence that has marred recent protests in the country, organisers were hoping for a "joyous and festive" occasion, reports France 24's Claire Paccalin from a march in Paris.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Shenzhen: Inside ‘China’s Silicon Valley’
stories.description: When Xi Jinping hosts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin at this year's APEC summit, he'll be doing it in one of his country's most technologically advanced cities. Shenzhen is China's premier hub for cutting-edge tech – a place where robo-taxis and AI-powered drones are a normal part of the background... Its current status is the result of decades of policies aimed at opening up the once communist country to international markets and foreign investment.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Deutsche Bank shares drop after reports exposing Epstein payments, Russia dealings
stories.description: Deutsche Bank shares fell more than 6% Tuesday after media reports based on leaked documents detailed the bank's dealings with clients including Russian oligarchs, US President Donald Trump and the late financier Jeffrey Epstein.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Serbia's student-backed MPs take seats in parliament after election win
stories.description: Serbia's Student ⁠List lawmakers entered parliament ​on Tuesday, cheered on by hundreds of supporters, after their October ​election victory ended 14 years of rule by the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS). The Student List, a group that includes academics, professionals, farmers, actors and activists ​chosen ‌by student assemblies, secured 140 seats in the ⁠250-member parliament in October 25 polls, while the SNS gained 104.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Trump says he takes possible Iran bomb threat to Washington 'very seriously'
stories.description: President Donald Trump said Tuesday that US authorities take any possible threats to Washington ‘very seriously’, following reports that Iran was planning to target senior Trump administration officials, possibly with a radioactive bomb. Tehran dismissed the reports as ‘fabricated’.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Urban Zulu and '100 Reasons to Stay Single in Lagos': Telling African stories on their own terms
stories.description: Africa's creative industries are attracting growing international attention, from fashion and film to television and music. But as African stories reach audiences around the world, a bigger question is emerging: who gets to tell those stories, and who gets to shape how the continent is seen? At FAME Week Africa in Cape Town, arts24 met some of the creatives driving that conversation.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: France's Le Pen promises to lower retirement age if she wins election
stories.description: French far-right ​leader Marine Le ​Pen vowed on Tuesday to repeal President ​Emmanuel ‌Macron's pension ⁠reform if she is ‌elected next spring and ⁠bring down the retirement age to ​60 to 62. She ‌also set out plans to ‌create a fund worth €900 ​billion ($990.54 billion) to help pay for pensions in ​the long term. It ​would take a generation ​to build up the fund, she added.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: France hit by fresh nationwide public sector strike
stories.description: Demonstrators gathered across France on Tuesday after unions called a nationwide strike by public sector workers in a bid to secure pay rises, despite government efforts to ease tensions as demonstrations roil the country.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Calls for cooperation as ASEAN summit awaits Trump
stories.description: The twice-yearly ASEAN summit of Southeast Asian nations is underway, with major global powers also descending upon the Philippines. It is a crucial moment for the region, as ASEAN leaders look to strengthen their influence and collaboration in an increasingly divided global landscape. The arrival of US President Donald Trump on Tuesday is also being welcomed as well as protested, as Charli James reports.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Estonia closes its border with Russia but can it keep Moscow out?
stories.description: Estonia announced this weekend it would close its border with Russia, after blaming its eastern neighbour of attempting to sabotage one of its drone factories. But at a time when the internet has become one of Russia’s most potent weapons to wage hybrid warfare, does closing the border even matter?
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'We're kind of at a stalemate': French government and unions 'dancing around each other'
stories.description: Amid continuing protests in France and tense negotiations between the government and trade unions, Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Paul Smith, Associate Professor in French and Francophone Studies at the University of Nottingham. “What's happening is that there are two parties kind of dancing around each other.” Smith explains that the government wants to delay negotiations until after trade union elections on 10 December, while the unions want an agreement as quickly as possible. With talks “more or less broken down” over a two-point difference in public sector pay proposals, he describes the situation as “kind of at a stalemate.”
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Did the US use ‘blackout bombs’ in Iran? Images reveal mysterious fibres at infrastructure sites
stories.description: Photographs published by Iranian local media suggest that US forces may have used graphite bombs, also known as ‘blackout bombs’, against infrastructure in Iran in recent days. These weapons are designed to disrupt electricity supplies by causing short circuits rather than physically destroying power facilities.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: French far-right candidate Le Pen vows to end Macron's pension reform if elected
stories.description: Far-right French presidential contender Marine Le Pen said Tuesday she would eliminate President Emmanuel Macron's pension reform, allowing hundreds of thousands of French workers to retire earlier, and create a new €900 billion retirement fund. The frontrunner in polls to win the presidential race is seeking to convince investors she can balance one of her most popular pledges with promises ​to restore order to ‌the public finances.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Singer-songwriter Mélissa Laveaux: 'Women need more positions of power in the music industry'
stories.description: One of France's top musical artists has spoken to FRANCE 24 about the need to empower more women in music. Mélissa Laveaux is currently taking part in the "Les Femmes s'en mêlent" or "Women get involved" festival, which is holding a series of events across the country in an initiative that started nearly 30 years ago and is still going today. The aim is to address the underrepresentation of female artists at music festivals. She spoke to us in Perspective.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Ukraine: Two bridges in Kyiv heavily damaged by Russian strikes
stories.description: Russia hit two major bridges in Kyiv while Ukraine struck Moscow's link to annexed Crimea for the second night in a row, officials said Tuesday, ahead of a historic meeting of Chinese, US and Russian leaders. Detals from the ground by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Kyiv, Gulliver Cragg.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Ukraine strikes major Russian bridge in Crimea with drones and missiles
stories.description: Ukrainian drones and missiles struck a vital bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Tuesday, calling it an “unprecedented” operation as Russia reported that its forces downed a record number of Ukrainian drones for the second straight day. Meanwhile, Russia struck two major bridges in Kyiv.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Ukraine, Russia hit key bridges ahead of Putin-Xi-Trump summit
stories.description: Ukraine struck Russia's Crimean bridge for the second night in a row on Tuesday, shutting it down, while Russia hit two major bridges in Kyiv -- the latest wave of attacks that come ahead of a historic meeting of the Chinese, US and Russian leaders.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Two Marseille drug traffickers sentenced to life in prison over triple murder
stories.description: Two figures in Marseille’s drug trafficking ring were sentenced to life in prison on Monday over a triple murder committed in 2020. Among the victims was Brahim Chabane, the older brother of anti-drug activist and deputy mayor of Marseille Amine Kessaci.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: 'Weirdo specialist' is the new Bond: Papers react to Robert Pattinson as 007
stories.description: PRESS REVIEW – Tuesday, November 17: European papers react to five EU countries' plan for a migrant expulsion centre in Rwanda. In other news, the Guardian reveals Israel's use of Amazon's cloud system for facial recognition in Gaza. Plus: the wait for the new James Bond is finally over.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: French presidential debate: 'Le Pen exposed xenophobic and authoritarian aspects of her policies'
stories.description: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Damien Lecomte, French political scientist, researcher, and lecturer at the University of Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne. With five months to go before France's presidential election, Marine Le Pen leads the opinion polls, while Jean-Luc Mélenchon emerges as her most likely second-round opponent. Lecomte says that "the other candidates are basically fighting for the second spot" and that the center and right are "desperately trying to find a way to avoid a second round" between the two. He also warns that a Le Pen presidency could "really change the political life with more xenophobic and nationalistic policies,"even if her ability to secure a parliamentary majority remains uncertain.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: COP31: Corporate interests gain access to govt delegations participating in climate negotiations
stories.description: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Siphesihle Mvundla, South African Climate and Energy Justice Campaigner at groundWork, a non-profit environmental justice organization. At COP31 in Turkey, representatives of major polluting industries have gained access to climate negotiations through government delegations, accredited organisations and other participation arrangements, according to research by the Kick Big Polluters Out coalition. Mvundla questions the extent of their involvement: "This year particularly, it's not just about the numbers, but it's about the influence that these private interests would have on the negotiations." While businesses have a role in implementing climate action, he questions their access to negotiations intended to regulate their industries and is calling for "an end to big polluter sponsorship and partnership at climate conferences" and insisted: "No more allowing big polluters to write the rules of climate action."
stories.subject: Science

stories.title: 🔴 Live: Kerch Bridge to occupied Crimea closed after Ukrainian strikes collapse road section
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: UEFA backs bid by France's Diallo to take on Infantino as FIFA chief
stories.description: UEFA has backed a bid by French Football Federation (FFF) President Philippe Diallo ⁠to run for ​the FIFA presidency in next March's election after Diallo emerged as an unexpected opponent to the current head of football's world governing body Gianni Infantino
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Third US aircraft carrier arrives in the Middle East as Iran targets Bahrain
stories.description: A third American aircraft carrier has arrived in the Middle East, US Central Command said in a social media post Monday, making a dramatic show of military might as President Donald Trump keeps his options open for next steps in the Iran war. It comes as Tehran said Sunday that its forces carried out a drone attack on a US radar system at a helicopter base in the Gulf kingdom of Bahrain.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Saudi Arabia replaces military commander after Yemen setbacks
stories.description: Saudi Arabia replaced the commander overseeing its coalition against Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis on Monday after Riyadh's Yemeni allies were forced to withdraw from swathes of territory in a major setback for their campaign against the group.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 5 European countries aim to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda
stories.description: A group of European countries announced Monday that they aim to set up a “return hub” in Rwanda where rejected asylum seekers could be sent from next year, a move that they hope will also deter more people from coming. The plan by Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece and the Netherlands, which have spearheaded negotiations with non-EU countries, drew immediate criticism from human rights groups.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Trump arrives in Philippines to kick off Asia trip
stories.description: US President Donald Trump arrived in the Philippines on Tuesday at the tail end of a Southeast Asian summit, with protests awaiting him as he prepares for the first meeting in two years of the Quad group of Indo-Pacific countries. France 24’s correspondent Tommy Walker has the details.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Candidates clash over cost of living in French presidential debate
stories.description: Five of the frontrunners for the French presidential election lined up for the second of this year's debates on Monday night. In an often-rowdy debate, candidates clashed over counterproposals to raise and cut taxes and slash public spending.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: France's far-right presidential candidate Le Pen to set out pension plans
stories.description: France's far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen is to set out pension proposals on Tuesday as she seeks to convince investors she can balance one of her most popular electoral pledges ‌with promises to restore order to the public finances. Le Pen’s National Rally (RN) has pledged to allow people ⁠who started work young to retire as early as 60, although it is under pressure to detail how it would ‌do this while also curbing budget deficits.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Russia receiving ‘dozens of missiles per month’ from North Korea, says Kyiv
stories.description: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said Monday that Russia was receiving "dozens of missiles per month" from North Korea and warned that the country was taking advantage of the war to make its weapons "more effective". He called on European allies to send more weapons so that Ukraine can respond "on equal terms" to the threat.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: China, Canada agree to further reduce tariffs at APEC summit in Shenzhen
stories.description: China is hosting the 21-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen this week, hoping to use the tech megalopolis to showcase its vision for international trade and development. The summit is also where the international agenda is enacted: Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney has met with his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping, with both leaders agreeing to reduce trade barriers between their countries. Also in this edition: Nvidia reportedly rejects a return of its former CEO Jensen Huang.
stories.subject: Business

stories.title: Data leak exposes Deutsche Bank ties to Russian oligarchs, Epstein and Trump
stories.description: Shares in Deutsche Bank plunged Tuesday after international media outlets published reports detailing the bank's questionable business practices over the past 20 years, including its ties to Russian oligarchs, convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and Donald Trump before he became the US president.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: AFCON 2027 qualifiers: Senegal beat Sudan and close in on qualification
stories.description: Senegal beat Sudan 4–2 on Matchday 4 of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers. Senegal top Group J and could secure qualification as early as Tuesday, November 17.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Live: France braces for new day of protests as unions call for nationwide strike
stories.description: France braced for another day of protests Tuesday as unions called for a nationwide strike by public sector workers in a bid to secure pay rises. Youth organisations and Yellow Vest activists are also set to join the demonstrations. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: New mass protests expected in France Tuesday as presidential election approaches
stories.description: Unions in France are calling for a strike Tuesday to demand wage increases, with students also expected to join. With under five months to go before the presidential election, FRANCE 24's Monte Francis asks Ariane Bogain, Senior Lecturer in French Politics at Northumbria University, what role the widespread discontent will play in the upcoming vote.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Macron visits Malaysia as France seeks closer defence and rare earths ties
stories.description: French President Emmanuel Macron will meet Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday to discuss strengthening defence, trade, energy and critical minerals co-operation. Macron's two-day visit, his first since 2017, comes ahead of the countries' 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations, with both sides seeking a strategic partnership.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Trump heads to Asia for historic nuclear talks with China and Russia
stories.description: US President Donald Trump headed to Asia on Monday for economic talks and a planned trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on nuclear issues and the war in Ukraine. Trump also raised the possibility of meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his visit.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: France Cricket federation faces collapse after funding scandal exposed by FRANCE 24
stories.description: France's national cricket organisation is on the verge of collapse, a top administrator says, three years after an explosive FRANCE 24 investigation revealed accusations that the body was faking matches to claim funds from the International Cricket Council.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Russian strikes hit two key bridges in Kyiv, disrupting water and power supplies
stories.description: Russian forces struck two major bridges crossing the Dnipro River in Kyiv late Monday, damaging critical infrastructure and causing water and power cuts in parts of the Ukrainian capital, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. The attacks came as Moscow launched a wider wave of drone and missile strikes across Ukraine, including in the regions of Cherkasy and Kharkiv.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Ukraine hits key Crimea bridge with drones
stories.description: "I think the Ukrainians are trying to send a message to the Russians with this - 'If you hit our bridges we can hit yours,'" reports Gulliver Cragg from Kyiv.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Chase outage disrupts online banking and Zelle payments in United States
stories.description: American users of several major banking apps and online portals reported outages on Monday, according to the monitoring site Downdetector.com, with one institution ruling out a cyberattack as the cause. Among those affected by the outages were Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase and the popular money transfer app Zelle.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: La Francophonie 'waning in global influence': Linguistic institutions becoming 'less important'
stories.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Phil Clark, professor of international politics at SOAS University of London. The diplomatic crisis between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo spilling out at the Francophonie summit in Phnom Penh for all to see has exposed an unexpected shift in their relations. Clark says that "nobody expected Rwanda to back down in this way" following President Macron's request that Paul Kagame withdraw Louise Mushikiwabo's candidacy for a third term.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Europe hunts for Palantir alternatives as militaries seek to limit US dependence
stories.description: As Europe's ​defence ministries look to limit dependency on American technology and major software company Palantir Technologies for critical military functions, a growing number of firms within the region are competing for their business. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Arthur Holland Michel, journalist and researcher specialising in emerging military technologies.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Europe hunts for Palantir alternatives as militaries seek to limit US dependence
stories.description: As Europe's ​defence ministries look to limit dependency on American technology and major software company Palantir Technologies for critical military functions, a growing number of firms within the region are competing for their business. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Arthur Holland Michel, journalist and researcher specialising in emerging military technologies.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Trump says he needs funding for air traffic control after ground stop
stories.description: US ​President ​Donald Trump, pressed on a ​technology ‌failure ⁠that ‌grounded thousands of ⁠flights last week, ​on ‌Monday told reporters ‌that ​the government needed funding for upgrade ​to ​air traffic ​control equipment. FRANCE 24's Monte Francis speaks with Sheldon Jacobson, Professor of Computer Science at the University of Illinois. He explains that "the Republicans have had full control of the House and the Senate since the President came in. They controlled everything. If they needed the money and wanted the money they could have approved the money. The fact that they didn't, in the the different bills that have been passed, suggests that it's more than just money that is going on here".
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Rogue AI: California sues OpenAI over "Hugging Face" and other cyberattacks
stories.description: The US state of California has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI over the "Hugging Face" and other cyberattacks, accusing the ChatGPT maker of knowingly testing dangerous advanced AI models without adequate safeguard. Meanwhile, the US Commerce Department has tightened rules over the export of US technology, aiming to close a loophole around remote access to advanced AI chips.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: US judge strikes down Trump visa restrictions on foreign students, journalists
stories.description: A US federal judge has struck down a Trump administration policy that would have sharply limited the length of time foreign students and journalists could stay in the country, ruling that the proposed restrictions were unlawful and would undermine opportunities for international education.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Rwanda to host hub for rejected EU migrants
stories.description: In tonight's edition, five European countries are negotiating a deal to deport rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda. Also, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda's political animosity spills over at the Francophonie Summit in Cambodia. And in Tunisia, young women are increasingly turning towards weightlifting and bodybuilding as a form of self-expression.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: November 17 blackout hoax: How a conspiracy theory went viral around the world
stories.description: A conspiracy theory claiming a worldwide “blackout” will hit on November 17 has spread across social media, cutting electricity, internet and banking services. The rumour stems from a routine US FEMA emergency alert test, but was amplified by cryptocurrency accounts, misleading claims about EU preparedness advice and references to The Simpsons. Recent technology outages, flight disruptions and cyberattacks have added to public anxiety, helping turn a routine test into a global blackout hoax.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Pope concludes South America homecoming, reassures faithful after cancer scare
stories.description: Pope Leo XIV finished Monday his 12-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru reiterating his advocacy for social justice, environmental protection and the importance of community. Just a month after undergoing lung cancer surgery, the 71-year-old pontiff drew millions of faithful across South America, where he spent nearly two decades as a missionary.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: The new faces of the US Congress
stories.description: The United States Congress is about to welcome dozens of new faces. A majority of them, Democratic, after the "blue wave" in the midterm elections. FRANCE 24's Washington correspondent Fraser Jackson catches up with one of these new lawmakers as they go through orientation as they prepare to take office in January. He speaks with Katy Padilla Stout, U.S. Representative-elect for Texas's 23rd congressional district.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Should Ukraine trade Donbas for NATO membership?
stories.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky asserting that the United States has asked him about a straight-up swap Russia gets the Donbas, the rest of Ukraine gets NATO membership, a guarantee against Moscow later having a second go and annexing the entire country. Whether or not the offer’s real, serious or that either side would accept it. We’ll ask if the talk of partition signals some kind of turning point in a nearly five-year war that's also a brutal stalemate.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: EU nations unveil Rwanda deal for migrant return hub
stories.description: Five EU countries including Germany and Denmark on Monday unveiled a deal to establish a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda -- the first such facility outside the bloc. The group, also comprising Austria, Greece and the Netherlands, has been gunning to open a "return-hub" despite rights groups' concerns, after the European Union cleared the way with a recent toughening of migration rules. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: UEFA backs France's Diallo to stand against Infantino in FIFA election
stories.description: European football's governing body UEFA has given its "unanimous" backing to French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino in March's FIFA presidential election, it said in a statement Monday. Under its Slovenian president Aleksander Ceferin, UEFA has led the opposition to Infantino since his announcement in late July of a project to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. FRANCE 24's Selina Sykes speaks with Dr. Emanuel Macedo de Medeiros, Co-founder and Global CEO of the Sport Integrity Global Alliance.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'A futuristic debate now very real': Why the world is struggling to regulate killer robots
stories.description: Representatives from 128 nations are meeting in Geneva on Monday to decide whether to move ahead with negotiating legally binding rules around the use of AI-powered weapons that can kill without human involvement. FRANCE 24 spoke with artificial intelligence researcher Vincent Boulanin to find out just what is at stake.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Czech mass protests: Media is the first casualty 'when you want to attack democracy'
stories.description: As hundreds of thousands of people gather in Prague to protest the Czech government's proposal to replace public broadcasting licence fees with direct state funding, Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Bára Stárek, Executive Director of Díky, že můžem. Stárek warns that the proposed changes offer "no real safeguards" against political influence, pointing to developments in Slovakia and Hungary. She also drew a parallel with the Velvet Revolution of 1989, recalling that "we didn't have a free media and we only had a state media" under communist rule. "Media is the first (line of) attack when you want to attack democracy," she said. With the legislation expected to reach Parliament in January, Stárek believes the demonstrations will continue if the government refuses to engage in any discussions.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Robert Pattinson: British actor will be the next James Bond
stories.description: British actor Robert Pattinson is set to become the next James Bond in the long-running 007 spy franchise. Discussions over the casting of the new James Bond had been going on for months, with Pattinson emerging as one of the frontrunners from the outset.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Russia's war on Ukraine: 'Americans want to have a deal whatever the cost for both Ukraine & Europe'
stories.description: Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Grégoire Roos, Director of the Europe and Russia and Eurasia Programmes at Chatham House. As European countries prepare to take part in the next round of Ukraine peace talks, Roos questions whether having five European representatives could weaken their negotiating position. "The other option is to realize that it dilutes the negotiating power of Europe. And I would lean towards that," he says, proposing Finnish President Alexander Stubb as a possible representative. Roos also points to differences between Washington and European governments over negotiations with Russia. While "the Americans do absolutely want to have a deal whatever the cost for both Ukraine and Europe," he argues that European governments have little choice but to maintain pressure on Moscow, which has yet to abandon its "maximalist demands."
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Robert Pattinson named as new James Bond
stories.description: British actor ​Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond, Amazon MGM Studios announced on Monday, ​taking on the role after Daniel Craig's departure from the long-running spy series.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: French film star Depardieu drops appeal against sexual conviction
stories.description: French film star Gérard Depardieu on Monday dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women during the filming of a movie in 2021 and issued "sincere apologies" for his past behaviour on set. "For a long time on film sets, I hid behind provocation and ribald humour," Depardieu, 77, said in the statement, withdrawing his appeal on the day it was set to go to trial. "I believed my remarks and some of my gestures would be without consequences" for those involved, he said. "They were not, particularly coming from a powerful figure such as I once was."
stories.subject: World

stories.title: French troops in Ukraine 'wouldn't be a surprise'
stories.description: French soldiers have been operating in Ukraine for several months, training Ukrainian troops and helping maintain military equipment, France 24's sister radio network Radio France Internationale (RFI) reported on Monday. While the deployment has not been confirmed, such a mission would not come as a surprise to many in Ukraine, reports France 24's correspondent in Kyiv Gulliver Cragg.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Prague: Thousands of Czechs rally against government media funding plan
stories.description: Tens of thousands of Czechs rallied in Prague on Sunday, November 15, against a government plan to cut a public media fee and move funding to the state budget, a policy critics say would dent the broadcasters' independence and viability.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Robert Pattinson named as new James Bond
stories.description: British actor Robert Pattinson, star of three mega-franchises, "The Batman", "Harry Potter" and "Twilight", has been named as the seventh 007. The announcement ends years of speculation about who would inherit the beloved role from Daniel Craig and comes five years after the last Bond release, "No Time to Die".
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Melissa Auf Der Maur: 90s rock memoirs and photographs
stories.description: Melissa Auf Der Maur grew up in Montreal, the daughter of a feminist activist mother and a journalist-turned-politician father. At just 22, she joined Courtney Love’s band Hole as its bass player, going on to become a role model for young female fans – and not only female fans – of alternative rock. She later joined The Smashing Pumpkins before striking out on her own as a solo artist. She dropped by FRANCE 24 to talk to Marjorie Hache about the epic decade that brought the 20th century to a close.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Verdict due in French trial over triple murder linked to Marseille drug wars
stories.description: In France, a highly anticipated verdict in a triple homicide is expected later today. Often called the Kessaci trial, the plight of the Kessaci family has drawn attention across France, the surviving brother Amine Kessaci has become an outspoken advocate against drug trafficking and in particular in Marseille.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Did France abandon its athletes after the Olympics?
stories.description: Two years after hosting the Olympics, France seems to have lost interest in supporting its athletes. With budget cuts and lackluster interest from sponsors, some – despite their competitive successes – are turning to influencer work to finance their sport careers.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: COP31 deal draft foreshadows difficult route to consensus
stories.description: COP31 negotiators in Turkey released a draft agreement on Monday to advance talks on fossil fuels and climate finance before this week's deadline. The pressure to reach a deal is intense after a year of environmental challenges including catastrophic glacier flooding in Nepal and European wildfires, even as global conflict and cost-of-living protests distract leaders from climate action.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Saudi Arabia dismisses commander of anti-Houthi coalition as rebels advance
stories.description: Saudi Arabia has removed the commander of the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen, state media said Monday, as the Iran-backed rebels advanced on the temporary capital of Aden. The shake up comes after Houthi forces took territory on Yemen's southern coast and Saudi-backed forces fell back to defend the capital.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'Historical fiction is about filling in the gaps', author Ian McGuire says
stories.description: A Man Booker Prize nominee has been speaking to FRANCE 24 about his latest novel and his passion for researching and writing historical fiction. Ian McGuire was shortlisted for the prize in 2016 for his novel “The North Water”. His latest book, “White River Crossing”, was published earlier this year and has now been translated into French, under the shortened title “White River”.
stories.subject: Science

stories.title: Musk among more than 150,000 calling for Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia
stories.description: Could Jensen Huang make a stunning return to Nvidia just days after resigning as CEO of the AI chip giant over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy? The possibility is growing after Elon Musk and more than 158,000 others signed an open letter calling for Huang's reinstatement.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: French troops 'deployed in Ukraine on secret mission'
stories.description: French soldiers have been operating in Ukraine for several months, training Ukrainian troops and helping maintain military equipment, France 24's sister radio network Radio France Internationale (RFI) reported on Monday. France 24's Douglas Herbert takes a closer look at the report's claims.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Russia says intercepted over 1,300 Ukrainian drones in a major attack
stories.description: Russia intercepted 1,336 drones launched by Ukraine, Russia’s Defense Ministry said Monday, in what was the most claimed downings since Moscow’s all-out invasion of its neighbor nearly five years ago. Russia, meanwhile, has battered Ukrainian civilian areas with relentless strikes that seek to choke the economy and break public morale, in attacks President Volodymyr Zelensky said were made possible ⁠partly due to restrictions on Ukraine's use of SpaceX's Starshield service.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Francophonie summit postpones new leader vote amid DR Congo-Rwanda dispute
stories.description: The Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie (OIF) on Monday had been set to choose its new secretary general during talks in the Cambodian capital Phnom Penh. But delegates decided to postpone the election for a year after a walkout threat by the Democratic Republic of Congo amid an ongoing dispute between Kinshasa and Kigali.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Verdict week in the Myanmar genocide case
stories.description: PRESS REVIEW – Monday, November 16: The international press looks ahead to a verdict that could find the state of Myanmar guilty of genocide against the Rohingya minority. In other news, French journalists lift the lid on the many trials involving child prostitution. And finally, in Ireland, a cache of 12,000 once-banned books is back in the spotlight.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Breaking taboos: Egypt's sexual revolution takes to social media
stories.description: In Egypt, a sexual revolution is quietly unfolding on social media. Accounts followed by tens of thousands of people, with posts attracting millions of views, are tackling a wide range of issues surrounding sexuality – from the widespread practice of female genital mutilation (which 93 per cent of women in rural areas have undergone) to sex education and sexual pleasure.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Xi, Trump and Putin to discuss 'world peace' at Shenzhen summit, China says
stories.description: The Chinese foreign ministry on Monday said that President Xi Jinping and his US and Russian counterparts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin would discuss "safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability" when they hold their first trilateral summit in Shenzhen this week. The meeting is expected to happen on Thursday on the sidelines of a summit of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Nations League: France defeat Turkey to advance to quarter-finals
stories.description: France struggled at times but defeated Turkey (2-1) in the Nations League matchday. France finished first in group A1 and qualified for the quarter-finals.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: 🔴 Live: 600 Ukrainian drones target Moscow, Crimea bridge strike halts traffic
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Five EU nations set to announce migrant deportation centre deal with Rwanda
stories.description: Five EU countries on Monday are set to announce a deal to establish a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda – the first such facility outside the bloc. The move comes after the EU toughened its migration rules in late 2025.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Eisenkot says Netanyahu ‘cannot remain’ after alleged election interference by aide
stories.description: Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot said on Sunday caretaker premier Benjamin Netanyahu must leave office immediately following reports of alleged electoral interference by a Netanyahu aide. The former army chief called Netanyahu and his entourage an immediate threat to democracy, hours after representatives discussed forming a national unity government.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs protest in Prague over public media funding plan
stories.description: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs rallied in Prague on Sunday against government plans to replace public media fees with direct state funding, which critics say threatens broadcasters’ independence. Organisers said turnout exceeded a March protest of more than 200,000, potentially making it the largest demonstration since the 1989 Velvet Revolution.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Elon Musk, Uber co-founder join calls to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia chief
stories.description: Elon Musk and an Uber co-founder were among more than 158,000 signatories by Sunday demanding Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia chief pending an independent investigation. Huang resigned Thursday after revelations of two extramarital affairs, one with a subordinate and another with a woman accused of spying for China, ending his 33-year tenure.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, architect of Mexico’s drug trade, dies aged 80
stories.description: Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, a founder of Mexico’s Guadalajara cartel known as the “boss of bosses”, died in hospital on Sunday aged 80 after suffering multiple organ failure, Jalisco state’s security ministry said. Imprisoned since 1989, he had been transferred from prison to the hospital two days before his death.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: Kroupi on target as France beat Turkey to reach Nations League quarters
stories.description: Eli Junior Kroupi scored his maiden goal for France as Les Bleus beat Turkey 2-1 in Bordeaux on Sunday to top their group with 13 points and qualify for the quarter-finals of the Nations League. World Cup winners Spain, who lost at home against England, are among their potential opponents in the last eight.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Nearly 2,200 migrants reach Spain's Canary Islands in two days
stories.description: Nearly 2,200 migrants have reached the Canary Islands over the past two days, Spain’s coastguard said Sunday, continuing a recent surge of arrivals from West African countries to the Spanish archipelago, where the authorities declared a migration emergency earlier this week.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Yemen's Houthis advance on Aden as government forces retreat to defend their capital
stories.description: Houthi forces in Yemen have advanced to within 60 kilometres of Aden, the seat of the country's internationally recognised government, military and government sources said Sunday. The embattled government earlier announced it was pulling back its last forces from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to defend its temporary capital on the southern coast of Yemen.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Pragues's fight for public TV - Why Renowned Presenter Will Leave Czech TV Over Reforms
stories.description: Daniel Stach, one of the Czech Republic’s best-known television presenters, tells Gavin Lee on France 24 why he is prepared to walk away from his career rather than work under changes that he says will threaten the independence of public broadcasting. As hundreds of thousands take to the streets of Prague, Stach explains why he is joining the protests against the government’s proposed overhaul of public media funding – and what is at stake for Czech television, journalism and democracy.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Estonia to close Russian border crossings after 'sabotage' attempt at drone factory
stories.description: Estonia will close all its border crossing points with Russia from December 1, its ​foreign minister ‌said on Sunday, following a suspected ⁠sabotage attack on an Estonian defence company that Tallinn blamed on ‌Moscow.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: How did over 2,000 migrants reach the Canaries in just 48 hours?
stories.description: Spain says nearly 2,200 migrants have arrived by boat to the Canary Islands this weekend. The strip of the Atlantic Ocean between West Africa and the Canary Islands is one of the world's deadliest migration routes – and the journey is usually made with ill-equipped dinghies and overcrowded boats. Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Madrid, Sarah Morris.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Israel kills senior member of Hamas's military wing in Gaza strike
stories.description: The Israeli military said on Sunday its forces had killed a senior member of Hamas's military wing in Gaza. The militant group confirmed the death of Samir Abu Younis, the commander of its Rafah brigade, adding that he played a prominent role in planning the October 7, 2023 attacks.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'Record number of women elected' to US Congress & governorships across country in midterm elections
stories.description: Following the 2026 US midterm elections, Gavin Lee is pleased to welcome Politico Senior National Politics Reporter Lauren Fedor. She discusses the growing number of Democratic women elected to Congress and governorships, particularly mothers of young children. “There was a realisation across the map that perhaps moms were the best messenger for this,” she explains, pointing to voters' concerns about “the cost of living, affordability, how to make ends meet.”
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Iran claims drone attack on US military base in Bahrain
stories.description: Bahrain issued two alerts of potential threats on Sunday, its first such warnings since September as blasts rocked the capital, Manama. It comes after Iran targeted an airbase in the US-allied island state, ending a long lull in strikes during the Middle East War and comes as negotiations to end the conflict remain at a stalemate, with the US maintaining its naval blockade and Iran its stranglehold over the strait of Hormuz. Story by Rachael Griffiths.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Canaries urge government action after 2,200 migrants reach the islands in 48h
stories.description: Spain says nearly 2,200 migrants have arrived by boat to the Canary Islands this weekend. The Spanish islands are one of the main entry points into Europe for migrants from Africa. The Spanish Interior Ministry says more than 13,000 arrived there between January and the end of last month. Details and analysis by Andrew Hilliar, FRANCE 24 international affairs editor.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Jensen Huang: The French Connection
stories.description: President Trump is heading to Asia in a few days time, and will meet President Putin and President Xi. There's likely to be one fewer tech giants at the table, Jensen Huang, newly resigned from Nvidia, over the suspected spy affair.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Santa school in full swing in London ahead of Christmas celebrations
stories.description: It may still be November but it's beginning to look a lot like Christmas in South London, as many Santa impersonators are heading to school for their festive training. The school, organised by an event company called Ministry of Fun, brings together Santas, elves, and Mrs Clauses to share experiences, practice belly laughs and learn how to bring the magic of Christmas to life. Story by Rachael Griffiths.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: A deep dive into Ivory Coast's solar energy goals
stories.description: Can Ivory Coast, which remains heavily dependent on fossil fuels, turn to solar power to make its energy consumption greener and more sustainable? We visited the country's new solar power plant in Ferkessédougou, in the north of the country. Inaugurated in July, it is expected to generate nearly 90 gigawatt-hours of electricity a year. Report by Julia Guggenheim.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Why the Nvidia scandal is bad news for Europe’s AI ambitions
stories.description: Nvidia's Jensen Huang poured money into open-source AI, from French-founded Hugging Face to chips for Mistral's data centres, and fought Washington's attempts to restrict it. With Huang gone and China hawks emboldened, Tech 24 asks whether Europe's AI ambitions have lost their most powerful ally, and whether he was ever the champion Europe needed.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: US probes nationwide flights stoppage as travel disruptions persist
stories.description: US air travel is expected to return to normal this Sunday, following a nationwide ground stop Friday night that stranded hundreds of thousands of passengers and disrupted travel worldwide. The Trump administration blamed the incident on a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines and said there was no evidence this was a cyberattack. The ground stop now raises questions about the country's aging infrastructure and lawmakers are calling for an investigation. Analysis by Philip Mann, aviation expert at Vector Strategic Consulting.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Chinese spy, chip sales, Trump ties... The Nvidia scandal deepens
stories.description: The Nvidia scandal continues to unravel. Sunday, the Singapore-based company Megaspeed said that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang had officially left the company in 2025. She is the alleged Chinese spy that had an affair with Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang. Late last year, revelations showed she was being investigated for chip smuggling. The scandal has also raised questions about how much the US government knew – Trump was allegedly warned about the affair but did not react. Analysis by Laïla Mörch, CEO of Shael and tech investor in Paris.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: The week in pictures: Spain protests, Pope Leo's Peru 'homecoming' and Rocky fans in Philly
stories.description: FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the week's most striking images, from angry protests over a housing crisis that has dominated Spain's election campaign, to Leo XIV's visit to his adopted homeland Peru and "Rocky" fans marking 50 years since the release of boxing movie classic.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: French Cyril Gane retains MMA heavyweaight title agianst Josh Hokit
stories.description: Ciryl Gane remains the world's MMA heavyweight champion. Overnight, the French athlete beat Josh Hokit in the main event of UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden in ​New York. The 5-round fight was rough, as Shirli Sitbon explains.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Bahrain says air defences destroyed several Iranian drones attacking US base
stories.description: Bahrain issued two alerts of potential threats on Sunday, its first such warnings since September. The second Iranian drone attack in three days, ending a long lull in strikes during the Middle East war. Diplomatic efforts to end the almost nine-month conflict have yet to produce a breakthrough, with ​sporadic attacks continuing. Details from the ground by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Tehran, Reza Sayah.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: France's presidential race heats up
stories.description: In approximately six months time, French voters will head to the polls for the first round of the presidential election. Due to term limits, current president Emmanuel Macron is barred from running again. But that hasn't stopped a whole host of candidates from tossing their hat in the ring.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Ukrainian drones strike Russia's petrochemical capital in overnight assault
stories.description: Russian officials confirmed Sunday that the central industrial city of Nizhnekamsk had endured "prolonged" Ukrainian airstrikes overnight, damaging a residential building and sparking a fire at a major petrochemical complex, injuring three people. Separate overnight strikes on Taganrog city killed an electricity substation engineer, according to the regional governor.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: The Philippines and Australia strengthen joint military deterrence at ASEAN summit
stories.description: Southeast Asian leaders opened their annual summit in the Philippine capital Manila on Sunday. During three days, world leaders are expected to focus on trade, energy and conflict – including the war in Iran. Donald Trump is expected to land in Manila on Tuesday. Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Bangkok Tommy Walker.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Will Ukraine make territorial concessions for NATO membership?
stories.description: The United States suggested Ukraine make territorial concessions in exchange for a NATO membership, according to Volodymyr Zelensky. The Ukrainian president also claims that Russia has rejected an energy truce. This week’s US-mediated negotiations did not result in any tangible progress. Story by Simon Moritz.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Air travel issues persist in the US after nationwide ground stop
stories.description: After almost five hours of grounded flights in the US, flights have resumed. However, passengers are still waiting and wading through tough logistics to get to their destinations after massive delays and cancelled flights. Details by Simon Moritz.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Francophone summit opens in Cambodia, overshadowed by tensions in Africa
stories.description: The 20th Francophonie Summit opened on Sunday in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, overshadowed by a high-stakes leadership dispute. The International Organisation of the Francophonie is set to elect its next secretary-general on Monday for a four-year term, but escalating friction between Rwanda, which has led the OIF for eight years, and the Democratic Republic of Congo has thrown the summit into crisis. Details by Liza Kaminov.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Illegal mining threatens French Guiana forests and indigenous communities
stories.description: In French Guiana, the fight against illegal gold mining is rapidly being lost and creating an environmental and health disaster, according to the World Wildlife Fund. During an aerial survey in early August, park rangers counted 239 illegal sites within the protected area in record.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Are we too reliant on technology? Questions arise after Microsoft's widespread outages
stories.description: This week's Microsoft outage highlighted the risks of relying on a single technology provider for essential services. The disruption lasted nearly 24 hours, impacting millions of users across more than 70 countries – from government agencies to airlines to hospitals and small businesses. Are we too reliant on technology? Analysis by Marcel Saucet, research associate at the University of San Diego School of Law.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Pope laments poverty-stricken Inca communities as locals leave Peru
stories.description: Pope Leo XIV on Sunday will traverse the length of Peru in what marks the penultimate day of his Latin American tour. The leader of the Catholic church – who underwent cancer surgery just a month ago – warned that Peru's remote Inca communities are under threat as poverty continues to drive locals out of their homeland in search of better futures.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Global diesel prices ease as winter approaches
stories.description: Global diesel prices, which have remained elevated since the start of the Iran war and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, have fallen sharply in recent weeks as Gulf exports recover and global oil supplies get back on track for the first time since February. The price drop is being felt in Europe, where prices remain roughly 77% above pre-war levels, and in the US, where the national average fell below $6 a gallon on Saturday. Details by Liza Kaminov.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Philippine star Carmelle wins first Asian edition of Eurovision song contest
stories.description: The Philippines has won the first Asian edition of the Eurovision Song Contest. The Filipino singer beat ten other acts to take the title in Bangkok, with a song celebrating women's empowerment. A taste of the winning song with Jack Pownall.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Iran claims attack on US military airbase in Bahrain
stories.description: Iranian military confirmed on Sunday an attack on a US military base in Bahrain, in its second targeting the Middle Eastern country in the space of three days. Bahrain's military said it had intercepted several Iranian attacks, with the foreign ministry confirming its air defence systems had shot down Iranian drones, preventing them from reaching their intended targets.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: SpaceX makes rocketry history by recapturing massive reusable rocketship
stories.description: After failing to catch a booster yesterday, SpaceX managed to recapture its massive reusable rocketship, "Starship" for the first time. Smaller previous models have successfully relanded but they require heavy legs and aren't fully reusable. Story by Daniel Quinlan.
stories.subject: Science

stories.title: Zinédine Zidane returns to Bordeaux as France take on Turkey in Nations League
stories.description: France will need to avoid defeat against Turkey, who they face in Bordeaux on Sunday night, to seal their spot in this season's Nations League quarter-finals. The match will see head coach Zinédine Zidane return to the city in which he spent four seasons as a player.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Three sentenced to death over Jordan church attack
stories.description: A Jordanian court on Sunday sentenced the three gunmen responsible for a terror attack on a church funeral procession in the village of Hamoud that killed nine and wounded others. The attack prompted retaliatory strikes on "terrorist organisations" in neighbouring Syria.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Cape Verde could make election history with first female president
stories.description: Cape Verde goes to the polls on Sunday in an election that could see the African island nation appoint its first ever female leader. Justice Minister Joana Rosa challenges incumbent Jose Maria Neves, who is the country's fifth president since it became independent from Portugal in 1975.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'Is this a cyberattack?' Grounded flights, a Microsoft outage and AI chaos fuel cybersecurity fears
stories.description: A series of unsettling disruptions, from tech stock turbulence and Microsoft outages to a nationwide grounding of flights, has left millions wondering whether the world’s increasingly interconnected technology systems are beginning to unravel.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: SpaceX's Starship completes first-ever mid-air catch after return from orbit
stories.description: SpaceX's Starship spacecraft made a successful return to Earth on Saturday, completing its first mid-air catch by giant robot arms in Texas, after an aborted recovery attempt.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Netanyahu renews call for Israeli government unity as Eisenkot dismisses 'tricks'
stories.description: Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday renewed his call for a national unity government with Gadi Eisenkot, who dismissed the appeal as a political ploy. This comes as the incoming premier is in the midst of negotiations to form a new administration.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Macron says limiting Ukraine aid would pave way to 'another war'
stories.description: French President Emmanuel Macron on Saturday warned that limiting aid to Ukraine would force Kyiv into an "unjust peace" and risk another war. His statement comes as the United States pushes ahead with efforts to negotiate between Ukraine and Moscow.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'No justice, no peace': Fifth round of protests sweep across France
stories.description: Between 106,000 and 200,000 people took to the streets across France on Saturday for the fifth round of protests, according to figures from the interior ministry and student unions respectively, as turnout fell and some incidents were reported.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Elon Musk's SpaceX aborts booster recovery due to technical issues
stories.description: Elon Musk's SpaceX is in the midst of a 15th test-flight of its Starship rocket. The company was hoping to pull off the first-ever "double catch" - with both the booster and the ship itself coming safely back down to earth. Instead, an unspecified problem forced the company to abort recovery of the booster, which was diverted from its return path and crashed down into the Gulf of Mexico.
